research.area: jeremy — Jeremy AI (jeremyhaynesai.com), its Utari / Utari Eternal platform, and comparable creator-AI-clone offers (as of 2026-10-27)

findings.title: Jeremy AI is now sold by application at $1,000/mo or $10,000/yr; an older instant-checkout flow is still in the site code
findings.detail: The live jeremyhaynesai.com homepage (single-page app; the same JS bundle is served for every route, checked 2026-10-27) leads with 'Apply Now'. That opens a Typeform application, then an 'Application Received' page that shows the price as $1,000/month or $10,000/year with status 'pending review'. It says a CSM will reach out by text, email or WhatsApp, onboard the buyer and help them write prompts for their business, and that team seats are discounted 'aggressively' as more users are added. The bundle still contains the older pages, which go straight to Whop checkout: /plans and /plans2 at $1,000/mo or $10,000/yr ('$833/month' billed annually, 'access in 60 seconds'), and /unlockjeremyai, an earlier long-form sales page. A /plans3 route shows $300/mo or $2,000/yr. The homepage does not link to it, and nothing says who it is for. Price anchors on the page: Inner Circle at $10K/mo, the agency at '$20K/mo plus revshare', and a single consulting call at $2,500+. Jeremy's blog gives the same $1,000/mo price and says access is by application.
findings.why_it_matters: This sets the price point for a creator-clone subscription in this niche: about $1K/mo, application-gated, with a CSM onboarding call. The move from instant checkout to an application suggests they want to qualify buyers and upsell rather than run a self-serve SaaS. That fits a white-label OS that a programme owner sells on to students and clients.

findings.title: Advertised channels: web, Telegram and SMS chat, a phone line with a cloned voice, and video calls (claimed)
findings.detail: The site describes 'Three ways to get mentored': (1) text on Telegram, web or SMS, pasting numbers, screenshots, scripts or ad copy, with answers claimed 'under 2 seconds'; (2) calling 'a real phone number' and talking to a low-latency cloned voice, 24/7; (3) team mode, where the bot is added to a Telegram group. The older onboarding copy also promises 'voice and video calling inside the portal'. The April 2026 launch post says video calling existed at launch, and that one customer kept it on a screen with a microphone so staff could walk up and talk to it. Images and screenshots are accepted as input, and memory of the business's context across conversations is claimed. Evidence so far: the sub-2-second latency, multilingual auto-translation and video calls are claims only. A vendor-made Arcade walkthrough does show a 'Start a voice call' button in the portal.
findings.why_it_matters: Voice by phone and Telegram group chat are what this audience now expects, and Jeremy used a phone-call demo reel as his best launch content. If Operator AI is web-only it will look weaker next to this.

sources.publisher: Arcade (vendor-made demo 'Getting Started With JeremyAI v1.0')

findings.title: The Jeremy AI portal on Utari has workers, triggers and skills alongside chat (shown in a vendor demo)
findings.detail: The public Arcade tour 'Getting Started With JeremyAI v1.0', embedded in the site code, steps through the customer UI: a main chat screen, a file-attach button, quick-action buttons for slides, docs, research, images and 'other common tasks', a voice-call button, chat history, and three navigation items. Those are 'Workers' ('focused helpers for specific jobs'), 'Triggers' ('set up automations') and 'Skills' ('help your workers do specific jobs'). This is stronger evidence than marketing copy, but it is still a vendor-made walkthrough, and nothing public shows what Jeremy AI's workers actually do.
findings.why_it_matters: Jeremy AI customers appear to get an agent workspace with automations, not just a chatbot. Operator AI's workers, triggers and skills model is matched on surface features, so the difference has to come from approval gates, role scoping and programme-specific workflows.

sources.publisher: Jeremy AI (bundle includes /test route embedding the demo)

findings.title: Team seats: the 'unlimited seats' claim conflicts with per-user pricing elsewhere on the same site
findings.detail: Feature cards on the site say 'Unlimited seats under one subscription' and invite users to add the bot to Telegram groups. The FAQ on the same site says to contact the CSM after purchase to discuss options and 'pricing for each user'. A third card says to 'Purchase seats for your team'. The application page says seat discounts grow with the number of users. The Utari blog post describes team mode as giving 'your whole team seats' so closers and operators can ask directly. Nothing public sets a fixed per-seat price.
findings.why_it_matters: Seat-based team access (closers, setters, ops) is a buying factor, and the vendor's own messaging is inconsistent. Operator AI can win on clear role-based seats for owner, coach, setter, closer and student.

findings.title: Claimed training corpus and daily Google Drive sync ('one day behind real Jeremy')
findings.detail: Claimed sources: 11,400+ hours of Zoom calls (1:1s, group calls, agency 'war rooms'), 85,000+ DMs and emails, 400+ SOPs and playbooks, 1,200+ Meta and Google ad-account audits, and 1,000+ paid course videos. Voice notes, community histories, mastermind sessions, Telegram, Slack and Facebook exports, and public YouTube and podcast content are also named. Jeremy says they export raw platform action logs (for example the Meta Ads Manager activity history) as training data, so the clone learns what was actually done, not only what was explained. A Google Drive folder syncs every day, so new material is claimed to reach the clone within about a day. The site says customer data 'stays in your workspace'. None of this is independently verified.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the moat as the vendor describes it: a private, constantly refreshed corpus plus action logs. Operator AI's knowledge-ingestion pipeline (Drive sync, call transcripts, DM exports, ad-account change logs) should meet this daily-freshness bar.

findings.title: 2026 change: Jeremy AI moved off Delphi (chat only) onto his own agentic Utari platform
findings.detail: Jeremy's own timeline: the first version ran from February 2025 as an internal and Inner Circle tool on Delphi, which he says cost about $25K a year. At the time he thought a $300/mo standalone price looked high. He promoted it from 28 March 2026, hit limits by 1 April, and launched it standalone 'around mid-April' 2026, tracking MRR from then. His 9 April post says Delphi's CEO declined to add agent functionality. By the 18 May post he had moved to Utari, ended Utari's self-serve product (honouring paid billing periods) and renamed it Utari Eternal. The site code still shows each stage: a Delphi chat embed (embed.delphi.ai) on /checkoutmim, login instructions for a Kajabi portal (jeremy-haynes.mykajabi.com), and a newer activation email from hey@utari.ai. Utari's own 3 April 2026 post still advertised self-serve 'Pro and Ultra' plans. So the 2 March post was rewritten later (its modified date is 28 August 2026).
findings.why_it_matters: The leading creator-clone in this niche dropped a chat-only clone vendor because customers wanted agentic execution. That supports Operator AI's agentic-OS thesis. It also shows that clones on third-party chat platforms are fragile.

findings.title: Limitations the vendor admitted: no file uploads, character caps, no link reading, churn, chat-only
findings.detail: Jeremy wrote that after launch he got 'numerous emails' saying the clone couldn't answer, with 'dozens' of failures in the first days. The causes he lists: links and URLs could not be processed; long transcripts were rejected for length (only after the user had typed them); PDFs, spreadsheets and slide decks were restricted or unsupported; and some subscribers churned because they wanted more advanced use. He also says it had no agentic function, so it could explain how to build webinar slides or a landing page but not build them. Utari Eternal now claims to remove these limits ('no character limits', 'any file type', 'share links'). Utari's January 2026 notes list 100MB uploads and documents read up to 150,000 characters.
findings.why_it_matters: These are now the minimum requirements for students and operators: long-transcript paste, file and link analysis, and execution. Missing any of them caused measurable churn for the category leader.

findings.title: Utari engine: role-scoped workers, per-worker knowledge, webhook, schedule and file triggers, broad integrations
findings.detail: Utari describes workers as agents with a defined role, such as auditing sales calls, monitoring CRM compliance or analysing ad accounts. Each worker sees only the slice of the knowledge base relevant to its job, and knowledge must be explicitly assigned to a worker. Triggers: webhooks from Fathom, Stripe, Typeform and others (January 2026); cron-style schedules, after a March 2026 fix for broken schedule triggers; and the example of a new transcript landing in a Drive folder. Integrations named: CRMs, Slack, Gmail, Stripe, ad platforms, Fathom, Fireflies, Webflow, Zendesk, Shopify, Notion, GitHub. Utari claims anything with an API can connect and that it has 'thousands' of connectors. Since March 2026 a worker can be created by describing it in plain English, and the AI writes the prompt and switches on integrations. Usage is billed in credits. Team workspaces (up to 3 members on the old Ultra plan) draw on the owner's credits.
findings.why_it_matters: This is very close to Operator AI's architecture (workers, triggers, skills, scoped knowledge). The comparison will turn on governance, role permissions and coaching-programme templates, not on raw automation.

findings.title: Call reviews run as autonomous Fathom-to-Slack workers, with no human approval step
findings.detail: Utari's official guide shows a 'Sales Call Analyzer' worker. A Fathom webhook fires when a call ends; the worker pulls the transcript and scores outcomes, next steps, call quality and red flags against an optional SOP or rubric, then posts the result to a Slack channel. The suggested prompt tells the agent not to ask questions and to start immediately. A similar Fireflies guide exists. Other features published without any visible review gate: January 2026 'bulk operations' such as sending emails to many recipients, and utari.ai's claim that the clone 'runs ad accounts, edits CRMs, builds reports'. No public material for Jeremy AI, Utari or Utari Eternal describes approval workflows or audit logs. A third-party review says SOC 2 and audit trails were not yet available.
findings.why_it_matters: This leaves room for Operator AI. Its approval-gated execution (draft, then human approve, then act, with audit) answers a governance gap in the closest competitor. That gap matters most for ad-account changes, outbound DMs and email, and CRM edits made for creator clients.

findings.title: Worker channels: email addresses that route to workers, bring-your-own Telegram bot, and Slack, with an allow-list of senders
findings.detail: Launched 3 April 2026. Email: each user gets an address at mail.utari.ai, plus 'workflow' addresses (for example research-, support- or content-) that send mail to a specific worker with custom instructions. Only approved senders can trigger a worker: the account email plus one more. Telegram: the user creates a bot through @BotFather, pastes in the token and picks a worker. It works in DMs and in groups when mentioned, accepts photos (read with vision), PDFs and other documents, and voice messages, and '/new' starts a fresh thread. Slack: one-click OAuth, DM or @mention, threaded replies, file parsing. Conversations from every channel appear in the dashboard with an icon showing the source. At launch this was limited to the self-serve Pro and Ultra plans.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a specific pattern for meeting setters, closers and students in the apps they already use. The sender allow-list is a useful safety pattern for Operator AI's channel connectors.

findings.title: Jeremy AI can be used inside Claude Code, Cursor and claude.ai through a hosted 'persona MCP'
findings.detail: On 5 July 2026 Utari shipped a hosted MCP connection. A user creates a token under Settings, then MCP, and connects Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop or claude.ai to their persona; the example command names the server 'jeremy-ai'. Memory and threads are shared between those tools and the dashboard. Tokens are scoped to one user and one persona, can be revoked, and expire after 90 days. It works for 'instance owners and community members', with usage billed to the instance owner. Testimonial screenshots on jeremyhaynesai.com mention a 'Jeremy MCP', Inner Circle members comparing Telegram with MCP, and a user plugging Jeremy AI into his own agent harness as a sparring partner.
findings.why_it_matters: Sophisticated operators want the expert brain available inside their own agent tools. Exposing Operator AI's coach or creator persona over MCP, with owner-pays billing, is a feature competitors already have.

findings.title: Custom MCPs returned with per-member credential isolation, after an earlier cross-user isolation bug
findings.detail: On 17 July 2026 Utari brought back custom MCP servers (HTTP or SSE) on workers. Tools are discovered automatically, credentials are encrypted at rest and never shown again, and each member's own connections stay private even on a shared worker. The example given is GoHighLevel 'or anything else that speaks MCP'. Utari says the feature had been paused while it reworked how credentials and member isolation work. The March 2026 notes list a fix for 'cross-user data isolation in Composio MCP integrations', and March also added custom MCP headers.
findings.why_it_matters: In a multi-tenant OS serving a programme's community, each student's or client's credentials need hard isolation. A competitor has already had to pause a feature and fix an isolation bug, which is a lesson for Operator AI's tenancy model and something to point out in sales.

findings.title: Audience Hub: synthetic focus groups that the clone summarises
findings.detail: Launched 1 July 2026. The user samples AI personas from an audience; three are seeded ('Digital Marketers', 'Investors', 'General Audience'), and custom audiences can be built from a one-line description that is expanded into a detailed brief. Up to 25 personas answer a question in character, then the user's Utari clone writes a synthesis and summary. Suggested uses: taglines, price points, landing-page hero copy, and ranking roadmap features. Also new in July 2026: reminders and notifications (in-app and email, with per-category settings), and editing and rerunning the last prompt (text only).
findings.why_it_matters: Growth operators test offers, hooks and VSL angles for creator clients. Synthetic audience testing ahead of ad spend is a feature Operator AI could match, framed as a hypothesis tool, not as evidence.

findings.title: Utari Eternal: a done-for-you agentic clone for coaches and experts at $25K/yr, by application
findings.detail: utari.ai now shows only an application ('Founding Cohort', 'v1.0', applications 'reviewed within 48 hours'). Jeremy's blog gives the price as $25,000 a year. It is aimed at experts, coaches with 'high-ticket programs', founders, creators, educators and agencies. Claims: the clone 'runs ad accounts, edits CRMs, builds reports'; takes phone calls in a cloned voice; translates in real time (Spanish, French, Russian, Mandarin are named); has 'thousands' of native connections; and has no character limits. It can be deployed on the web, by phone or SMS, embedded in the expert's products, or sold as a standalone offer, where it 'answers, executes, upsells, and supports 24/7'. The process has three stages: sync (calls, courses, DMs, voice notes, SOPs); train and refine (turn expertise into agentic skills built from skill.md files, clone the voice, QA); and deploy. Jeremy says 'dozens' of clients have moved forward. Jeremy AI is the public case study. Utari also still advertises separate custom 'Enterprise AI Workers' implementation with custom pricing. A 30 March 2026 post said 'personalized AI instances with custom subdomains' were coming, which amounts to white-labelling.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the most direct competitor to Operator AI's white-label positioning: an expert's clone with agent abilities, sold to that expert's students and clients. It sets an anchor of about $25K a year for setup and hosting.

findings.title: 'Instances': scoped clones for webinars, challenges, internal teams and sales-page trials, with usage caps
findings.detail: Jeremy describes 'instances': separate deployments of the clone, each limited to part of the knowledge base. Examples: a limited-time instance for webinar attendees trained only on that webinar; a client's 3-day-challenge instance used for retention and limited to stop abuse; an internal team instance that staff (marketing, editors, executives, assistants) use before taking up his time; and a sales-page instance where a visitor enters an email, gets a code, and is allowed a set number of messages or minutes of talk time. That one has IP blocking that detects VPN rotation. He also says instances have been brought into live sales calls as demos, used as setters, and deployed in Telegram and Slack channels.
findings.why_it_matters: This maps onto Operator AI's roles and funnel: a limited trial clone in the VSL or webinar funnel, a student-only instance, and a team instance. Knowledge scoping, metering and anti-abuse controls belong in the product.

findings.title: Usage and revenue claims are large, unverified and inconsistent between the vendor's own pages
findings.detail: Figures the vendor publishes: 400,000+ messages in the first 12 months, from users in 100+ countries; Jeremy AI revenue of more than $60K/month, which utari.ai also gives as a '$700K+/year' stream. The figures conflict. '129K+' messages is described as 'the day it rolled out' in the Utari post, labelled 'First Week' but captioned 'day-one rollout' on utari.ai, and given as 'the most recent 30 days' (with 2,200+ threads) in the 18 May post. The same 18 May post says both '440,000 messages / 28,000 threads over 12 months' and 'over 11,000 conversation threads' from February 2025 to February 2026. For the last 30 days on the old Delphi system it gives 270 users, 89,530 messages and about 4 minutes per conversation. Voice is said to log 'thousands of minutes per month'. Inner Circle members and students on the 7-week course also have access, so message counts are not counts of paying subscribers.
findings.why_it_matters: These give rough benchmarks for engagement with a creator clone in a coaching community: hundreds of active users and tens of thousands of messages a month. They should not be used as verified market data or in Operator AI marketing.

findings.title: Advertised use cases are advisory and asset-drafting; ad-account changes, DM or email review and outreach are not shown for Jeremy AI
findings.detail: jeremyhaynesai.com lists: auditing Meta ads from a pasted Ads Manager screenshot; diagnosing a funnel; writing setter scripts, credibility emails, ad hooks, VSL and short-form scripts, offer reframes, show-up stacks, follow-ups and collections or dunning policies; modelling ROAS, CAC, AOV and cash collected; job specs, SOPs and pipeline rules; and campaign planning. Examples of first-week questions carry 'answered in 0.8–1.4s' labels. It sells ROI levers such as +10% show rate, +5% close rate and lower cost per result. The link-in-bio page says it 'builds ads, VSLs, pages and emails, and audits what you're already running'. In the public material, 'audits' and 'reviews' are users pasting screenshots or transcripts into chat. No direct ad-account or CRM write actions, live DM or email inbox review, automated outreach, or student onboarding automation are shown for Jeremy AI itself. utari.ai claims ad-account and CRM execution in general terms only.
findings.why_it_matters: Execution-level, approval-gated agents for DM setting, ad changes and fulfilment are not publicly demonstrated by the closest competitor. That is Operator AI's clearest opening.

findings.title: Onboarding is a starter-prompt checklist, a CSM call and a 90-day prompt email sequence, bundled into the coaching programmes
findings.detail: After purchase, buyers see 'Getting started: 6 things to do right now', six ready-made tasks (ad audit, setter script, credibility email, funnel diagnosis using the 'Three-Part Bridge', hooks using the 'CPO framework', campaign plan), and are told that more prompts and use cases will follow by email over the coming weeks. Jeremy says he got past his worry that buyers needed his full course to get value by building a 90-day onboarding email sequence of the best prompts. Access is also bundled for Inner Circle members and students of the 7-week Master Internet Marketing course. A named support contact and a CSM handle setup. The legacy flow logged users in through a Kajabi course portal.
findings.why_it_matters: Students struggle to ask good questions. Guided prompt libraries tied to the programme's frameworks, and onboarding sequences, are needed to drive activation and retention. Operator AI's student role should ship with framework-tagged starter tasks.

findings.title: Free lead magnets around Jeremy AI: a 90-day scaling plan and 38 downloadable agent-skill files
findings.detail: scalingplans.com, linked from Jeremy's link-in-bio page, offers a free 'Try JeremyAI' plan. The user fills in a Typeform (about 5 minutes, no follow-up questions) and gets an emailed 90-day plan with reverse-engineered revenue maths (AOV, close rate, show rate, cost per call, ad spend), the single binding constraint, prioritised levers, week-by-week targets, the 'mistake to avoid' and a 'Phase 2'. jeremyhaynes.com/skills hosts 38 public agent-skill files in Markdown (call funnel blueprint, coaching delivery model, creative micro-tests and others), last synced 30 March 2026. Jeremy says the skills are email-gated and lead to a sales page for the full clone, and that people who decline are offered his agent platform instead.
findings.why_it_matters: This shows how an AI-diagnostic lead magnet feeds a high-ticket offer. Operator AI's growth-operator students could use the same pattern for creator clients, and an Operator AI version should keep the quality of what goes out under human review.

findings.title: Public feedback is almost entirely vendor-curated testimonials; no independent reviews of Jeremy AI were found
findings.detail: jeremyhaynesai.com shows about 35 screenshot testimonials from Telegram, group chats and DMs, presented as 'unedited'. Recurring themes in the captions: catching ad-account errors (a campaign objective silently changed when a campaign was duplicated, a pixel feeding back unqualified leads); using it as a 'setter manager' or sales manager; critiques of pricing and offers; building VSLs, ads, opt-in pages and email sequences within hours; ROI stories (for example a booking rate moving from 7% to 25%); plugging it into MCP or agent harnesses; and one user preferring it to 'Hormozi AI'. All are selected by the vendor. The on-site 'Write a Review' widget showed 'No reviews yet', and its submissions go to a Zapier webhook with an admin moderation page. Searches found no Reddit, Trustpilot or Product Hunt reviews of Jeremy AI. One public X post (26 January 2026) from a programme-adjacent user praised Utari for building two internal agents in a weekend. Jeremy himself reports early complaints and churn (see the limitations finding).
findings.why_it_matters: The claimed outcomes cannot be independently verified. Operator AI should expect prospects to arrive with expectations set by these testimonials, and should collect and publish verifiable usage and outcome data of its own.

sources.publisher: X (user post, seen via search snippet)

findings.title: Third-party review of the old self-serve Utari: works for simple tasks, struggles with vague instructions, no audit trail
findings.detail: Agent Finder (published 28 May 2026, updated 13 July 2026; it says AI tools helped draft the review) tested Utari for 12 days and scored it 7/10. Its points: writing good worker instructions takes practice; vague instructions give vague results; workers do not learn from corrections, so instructions must be edited by hand; about 30% of email drafts needed editing; a CRM-monitoring worker flagged 14 of 15 stalled deals with one false positive; and SOC 2 and audit trails were not available. The prices it lists ($0, $29, $79 and Enterprise) do not match Jeremy's ($20, $50, $200 plus a free tier) or Utari's own 'Pro and Ultra' plan names, so its facts are unreliable.
findings.why_it_matters: Even this low-quality review points to the same gaps Operator AI can address: learning from corrections, approval and audit trails, and compliance posture.

findings.title: Technical lineage and stack: Utari says it is renamed open-source Suna and moved to AWS in March 2026
findings.detail: A utari.ai/suna page says Utari is 'the evolution of Suna' under a new name and domain, with 'all your existing agents and workflows' unchanged. It points to a GitHub repo that returned not-found on 27 October 2026. Third-party sources describe Suna as Kortix AI's open-source generalist agent, licensed Apache-2.0 (not verified against the LICENSE file). On 30 March 2026 Utari moved from a single Railway server to AWS (load balancer plus auto-scaling Fargate, at least 2 servers across availability zones, a 10-minute idle timeout for streamed responses, and a new webhook base URL). January 2026 notes mention the Veo 3.1 video model, the Nano Banana Pro image model, and canvas and diagram generation. Utari's docs (docs.utari.ai), including 'Getting Started With JeremyAI', now redirect to a login page.
findings.why_it_matters: The competitor's agent core appears to come from an open-source project, so its edge is the corpus, the packaging and the distribution, not proprietary agent technology. Its docs are no longer public, which limits outside verification.

findings.title: Comparable: Hormozi's ACQ AI inside ACQ Vantage, invitation-only, priced from $1K/mo to $36K/yr
findings.detail: Acquisition.com's ACQ Vantage page, which a Jeremy AI testimonial calls 'Hormozi AI', describes ACQ AI as the diagnosis it runs on portfolio companies 'turned into software'. Members enter their numbers, and it names the constraint and points to a playbook. The training-data figure is inconsistent on the page: '50k hours of consulting' in one place, 'roughly 40,000 hours' from 2,000+ consults in another. The structured data lists Standard Monthly at $1,000, Premium Annual at $8,000, VIP Monthly at $3,000 and VIP Annual at $36,000; the visible VIP tier includes 'ACQ AI PRO (Unlimited Access)'. The page also describes an invitation-only Skool community of verified $1M+ operators and trainings on 'Integration with Claude + Fathom'. Member testimonials describe pasting in a website and having Claude Code carry out ACQ AI's suggestions. No voice or agent features are advertised.
findings.why_it_matters: Two major high-ticket creators now sell an expert AI at about $1K/mo or bundled into a membership. Diagnosing the constraint from the user's numbers is the expected core feature.

findings.title: Comparable: Delphi, the clone platform Jeremy left, now lists 'actions', voice, and WhatsApp on its top tier
findings.detail: Delphi's pricing page (delphi.co, © 2026) lists Scaler at $5k/yr (10 integrations, 'pro voice calls', 12M training words, 'actions and developer platform', Slack), Scaler + API at $10k/yr (API, SSO, 20M words, unlimited integrations, 60-day onboarding), and Immortal at custom pricing (text and WhatsApp, custom apps, unlimited words). Jeremy said in May 2026 that Delphi had no plans for agentic functionality and charged him $25K/yr. The newer 'actions' line suggests Delphi may be closing that gap; how far its actions go was not verified.
findings.why_it_matters: Clone-hosting prices run from about $5K to $25K a year, and chat-only clone vendors are adding actions. Operator AI's agentic advantage may not last without workflows specific to growth operators and governance.

findings.title: Comparable: a Robbins/Graziosi bootcamp teaches coaching buyers to build their own clone
findings.detail: The 'AI Advantage Bootcamp' sales page, credited to Tony Robbins, Dean Graziosi and their head of AI education, sells a 'Clone Builder System': workshop 1 builds a clone 'in one session' from the buyer's goals, values and writing, and workshop 5 turns it into an agent. Prices on the page are inconsistent ($995, or 3 payments of $380; $745; $797 and $1,197 packages). It promises '15+ hours a week' back or a refund, and lists an in-person event in Phoenix on 8–10 July 2026. The page contains placeholder and test text, so details are unreliable.
findings.why_it_matters: Mass-market coaching brands are teaching buyers to build their own clones. That pushes down the perceived value of a generic clone and favours Operator AI's role-specific, approval-gated workflows.

findings.title: Programme expectation: an Inner Circle case study runs an AI setter stack end to end, with a human only at the close
findings.detail: Jeremy's 13 April 2026 post (promoted on X on 8 June 2026 as a '$10M/year business with ZERO employees') describes an Inner Circle member's setup. A Meta instant form with conditional budget questions and free-text answers feeds an AI setter running on Claude Opus. The setter texts through SendBlue (BlueBubbles was tried) and calls with an ElevenLabs voice (Bland had lower latency, ElevenLabs better answers). It qualifies leads against a Notion 'war room' of sales calls sorted good, bad and average, plus live inventory. It moves Salesforce pipeline stages, writes personalised email sequences, raises QuickBooks quotes and invoices, works an Asana task queue, and hands qualified leads to the owner through a three-way text. This is a member's custom build, not a Jeremy AI feature.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the end-to-end setter, CRM, invoicing and handoff flow that programme members are now shown as achievable. Operator AI's setter and closer roles need the same pieces, with approval gates, compliance checks and a clean human handoff.

open_questions: What do Jeremy AI's workers, triggers and skills do for a $1K/mo subscriber in practice? The Arcade demo shows the menus but not any pre-built workers. Can subscribers connect their own Meta Ads, GoHighLevel or CRM accounts and let it write changes?

Does Jeremy AI or Utari Eternal have any approval step, audit log or role permissions before agent actions such as ad edits, CRM updates or bulk email? Nothing public describes one, and docs.utari.ai is now behind a login.
Is the $300/mo or $2,000/yr plan at /plans3 a live offer (student, Inner Circle or downsell pricing) or a leftover from the February 2025 pricing test?
How are team seats priced in practice: unlimited under one subscription, or per user through the CSM? The site says both.
Which phone and voice stack powers the cloned voice line? Is the video call still offered after the move to Utari? Is the claimed multilingual auto-translation live for Jeremy AI?
Real current subscriber count and churn: the $60K+/month revenue and the usage figures are inconsistent, and Inner Circle and 7-week course students also have access.
Is the GitHub repo cited for the Utari/Suna lineage public anywhere, and does Utari Eternal still run on a Suna (Kortix) fork?
Are there independent customer reviews on YouTube comments, Skool, Telegram communities or other forums that public search does not index?
Has Utari Eternal shipped the promised white-label 'personalized AI instances with custom subdomains' for clients other than Jeremy, and at what price above the $25K/yr base?

findings.title: Delphi (AI expert clone): voice/video 'digital minds' now sold as annual plans; monetisation is not built in
findings.detail: Delphi's official pricing page (no date on page; fetched 2026-10-27) lists only annual plans: Scaler at $5k/yr (10 integrations, 'Pro voice calls', 12M training words, Actions & developer platform, Slack, product recommendations), Scaler + API at $10k/yr (API, SSO, unlimited integrations, 20M words) and a custom-priced Immortal tier (Text and WhatsApp, custom applications, 'advanced mind architecture'). A third-party review dated 2026-09-11 recorded different prices: Free, Builder $79/mo, Scaler $299/mo, Immortal custom. That suggests a recent move upmarket, but this is not confirmed. Features users value: training on a creator's corpus (site, Substack, podcast, YouTube, files) that keeps updating; citations back to sources; editing an answer to save it as a Q&A correction; analytics on what the audience asks; lead capture; access groups and CSV contact import; voice and video calls. Cerebras (2025-03-26) also lists SMS, WhatsApp, Zoom, Slack and Discord as channels. Per that review, Delphi's help center says monetisation is 'not built in': creators link out to their own checkout, and the only recurring payout documented is a 30%/24-month referral programme. findings.why_it_matters: Delphi sets the quality bar for an expert's 'digital mind': grounded answers, citations, voice/video, and analytics on audience questions. Its gaps are native paywalling and anything downstream of the conversation (setting, booking, fulfilment). Operator AI can fill those for creator clients.

findings.title: Kajabi went 'AI operating system' in 2026: Cofounder, a drafts-only MCP and paid Expert Agents

Kajabi Payments fees run from 2.9% + $0.30 to 2.7% + $0.30, and fees on third-party processors are 2%, 1% or 0.5%. findings.why_it_matters: Buyers now expect practice, real-call scoring, targeted re-practice and live in-call help in one loop. Operator AI's closer and setter training for students should connect roleplay scores to real call reviews rather than sit standalone.

findings.title: Second Nature: enterprise roleplay adds file-to-roleplay generation, multi-persona sessions, a no-score practice mode and (reportedly) video avatars
findings.detail: Second Nature's official Q4-2025 update (posted 2025-12-20, updated 2026-01-20) covers: multi-persona roleplays with several stakeholders in one session; uploading a file to auto-generate a complete roleplay, with voice choice and an auto-selected avatar (building on a voice-command roleplay builder from Q2 2025); a Practice Mode with no scores, real-time feedback and in-conversation hints; and reporting API exports (JSON/CSV/xlsx). A competitor review (Outdoo, updated 2026-10-17) reports video-avatar roleplay added July 2026, English-only and single-persona at first. The same review cites a vendor quote of $50 per credit (one user-month) and third-party estimates of $30–40/seat/month with a roughly $20K annual minimum. Valued features: auto-scoring, LMS/SSO/Salesforce integrations, certification tracking, SOC 2/ISO certifications. 2026 awards: Webby Honoree (2026-04-21) and We Love Tech (2026-05-13). It raised $22M in Oct 2025.
findings.why_it_matters: Generating a roleplay from an uploaded script or offer doc, and a low-stakes practice mode with hints, are now expected features. Both suit students rehearsing setter and closer scripts for a creator's offer.

findings.title: GoHighLevel AI Employee: official per-location AI pricing (pay-per-use / $50 / $97) with metered voice and token costs
findings.detail: HighLevel's help article (modified 2026-10-20) sets three tiers per enabled location. Pay-per-use has no monthly fee. AI Employee Growth is $50/mo: 1,000 Conversation AI responses and 100 Voice AI minutes, then pay-per-use. AI Employee Unlimited is $97/mo: Conversation and Voice AI unlimited under fair use. Reviews AI and Content AI are unlimited on both paid tiers (pay-per-use rates: $0.01 per review reply; $0.063/image; $0.0945 per 1K words). Funnel AI is free up to 1,000 prompts/day. Agent Studio is always billed at token cost and is in no plan. Ask AI usage is included, 3x on Unlimited. Voice pay-per-use: engine $0.045/min from 2026-05-20, plus TTS (OpenAI/Cartesia $0.015/min, ElevenLabs V2.5 $0.035, ElevenLabs V3 $0.17) and LLM tokens. Speech-to-speech is $0.10/min (Gemini 3.1 Flash Live preview) or $0.20/min (gpt-realtime-2). All of this is on top of base plans of $97, $297 or $497/mo. Third-party guides date the Unlimited/Growth repackaging to Feb 2026, and Voice AI transcription in 10 languages with auto-detection to Mar 2026. Valued features: 24/7 SMS/IG/FB/WhatsApp replies that book into the calendar, inbound/outbound voice agents, review replies, a visual Agent Studio builder.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the default AI-setter price anchor for the agency/growth-operator market. Students will compare Operator AI's per-client cost with $50–97 per location plus usage, and many creator clients already run on GHL.

findings.title: HighLevel MCP server: external agents can act inside the CRM (book, follow up, move pipeline) with scoped tokens
findings.detail: HighLevel launched an official MCP server on 2025-07-30 (press release 2025-07-28). It started with 21 tools across Calendars, Contacts, Conversations, Pipelines and Payments, with a target of 250+ tools by the end of 2025. Agents can book appointments, follow up with leads, update records, move deals through stages and pull transactions without a human logging in. Access uses Private Integration Tokens with scoped permissions (endpoint documented in the help centre). Later, HighLevel's workflow 'AI Agent' action was able to call external MCP servers, so traffic goes both ways.
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI can integrate with clients' GHL accounts through MCP instead of building custom integrations. The approval gate must sit on Operator AI's side, because GHL's scoped tokens grant capability but do not require per-action human approval.

findings.title: CloseBot and DM-native AI setters: cheap, CRM-attached qualifiers, and per a vendor round-up none has a human-approval step
findings.detail: CloseBot runs on top of GoHighLevel or HubSpot rather than connecting to Instagram directly. Plans: Free (100 messages/mo, 1 agent), Business from $64/mo ($53 annual), Agency $397/mo ($331 annual) plus about $0.012 per message rebilled. CloseBot's blog flagged message-pricing changes for 2026-06-30. Capabilities: agentic AI with tools, built-in follow-ups, CRM calendar booking, any CRM-connected channel. The SetSmart round-up (prices checked 2026-09-20; vendor-authored) lists SetSmart ($97/mo for 1,000 messages; IG/WhatsApp/Messenger; in-chat booking, voice notes, auto follow-ups at about 4h and 23h), Setter AI ($49–499/mo by lead volume; SMS/WhatsApp/web), Appointwise ($97–297, needs GHL), InstantDM and Inrō (cheap comment-to-DM tools for Instagram). The round-up states that none of the six offers a human-approval step. SetSmart's self-reported benchmark from 828K DM conversations: 22.9% of engaged leads qualified and 1.94% booked into calls (vendor claim). Human setters are commonly cited at $2,000–4,000/month.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the most direct competitor set for Operator AI's setter role. Their weak points (no approval gate, no shared memory with closer and coach, no compliance tooling) are where Operator AI can differ. The vendor-reported booking rates give a rough benchmark to compare against.

findings.title: Meta Business Agent (June 2026): a free, native AI setter in WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger that books appointments and qualifies leads
findings.detail: Meta launched Business Agent globally on 2026-06-03 at its Conversations conference. It extends an agent already used by more than one million businesses on WhatsApp and Messenger to Instagram. It answers questions, recommends products, books appointments, qualifies leads, works to close sales, replies in local languages and summarises chats, and the business decides when a human takes over. A Business Agent Platform for custom agents connects to Shopify, Zendesk and similar systems, with enterprise guardrails and measurement. It is free at launch, with a paid subscription and token-based charges for larger businesses to follow. Reports differ on timing.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a platform-native substitute for third-party DM setters. Operator AI's setter value has to come from offer-specific qualification, shared context with closers and coaches, approval gates and attribution, not basic DM auto-reply. Meta also controls the API rules (see the messaging-window finding).

findings.title: Instagram/Messenger API rules constrain every AI setter: 24-hour automation window, Human Agent tag for humans only, no cold DMs
findings.detail: Third-party developer guides consistently report these rules. Automated or promotional replies are allowed only within 24 hours of the user's last message, and each new message resets the window. The HUMAN_AGENT tag extends this to 7 days, needs its own App Review, and is for human agents only, not bot messages. The API cannot start conversations, so cold outreach is not possible. Violations can lead to warnings, feature restrictions or messaging blocks. Two guides report that the CONFIRMED_EVENT_UPDATE tag was retired on 2026-04-27. Meta's own developer documentation was not fetched to confirm the details.
findings.why_it_matters: An approval-gated setter fits these rules well. Bot replies inside 24 hours can be automated; follow-ups after 24 hours should go to a human setter for approval or sending, which matches Operator AI's setter role. Compliance-aware follow-up scheduling would set it apart from setters that ignore the window.

findings.title: Instantly: AI Sales Agent (March 2026) offers human-in-the-loop or autopilot modes; AI Reply Agent answers within 5 minutes
findings.detail: The official changelog dates the AI Sales Agent to 2026-03-26. Given only a URL, it finds ICP-matched buyers, enriches leads, writes outreach and follows up. Work appears in an Activity Feed, with a choice of Human-in-the-loop (review before going live) or Autopilot. The AI Reply Agent (2025-07-15) aims to reply in under 5 minutes 24/7, shares booking links and pings Slack. Pricing page (fetched 2026-10-27): bundles Starter $94/mo ($85 annual; 5K emails, 1,500 credits, AI Sales Agent), Scale $194 ($175; 100K emails, AI Reply Agent, Unibox, advanced deliverability) and Agency $555 ($500; 500K emails, SISR server/IP sharding and rotation). The standalone Outreach plan starts at $47 ($37.60) with unlimited mailboxes and warmup. There is also a 450M+ lead database, waterfall enrichment across 5+ providers, a web-researcher agent and bring-your-own LLM key. The '4.2M+ account warmup network' figure is a vendor claim.
findings.why_it_matters: Outbound tools now offer an explicit choice between review-first and autopilot modes. Operator AI's approval-gating should be configurable per action type in the same way, so students can move a client from review to autopilot as trust builds.

findings.title: Smartlead: SmartAgents (Feb 2026), email + LinkedIn in one flow, and white-label client workspaces for agencies
findings.detail: The official changelog dates SmartAgents to 2026-02-09. These no-code AI operators create and manage campaigns, handle replies, sync with CRM and LinkedIn, and monitor mailbox health. A 2026-01-21 update put email and LinkedIn in one system with shared data. A third-party directory also lists SmartDialer, SmartProspect and a SmartCLI in March 2026. Pricing page (fetched 2026-10-27): Base $39/mo ($32 annual; 6K sends), Pro $94 ($78; 90K), Unlimited Smart $174 ($144; 150K), Unlimited Prime $379 ($315; 500K, 3 SmartServers, 3+ client workspaces). All plans allow unlimited mailboxes. White-labelling costs $29 per client workspace per month. Add-ons: SmartDelivery placement testing ($49–599/mo) and dedicated-IP SmartServers ($39 each). API and webhooks are listed.
findings.why_it_matters: Agency-style white-label client workspaces are table stakes for tools sold to growth operators who run several creator clients. Operator AI's white-label and multi-client model will be compared with $29 per workspace.

findings.title: lemlist: lemAgent builds a whole multichannel campaign from a conversation, keeps memory of past results, and the user reviews it before launch; MCP and CLI included
findings.detail: Pricing page (fetched 2026-10-27): Email $69/mo ($55 annual; 50K emails, 650M+ lead database, warm-up and deliverability hub, CRM integrations/API) and Multichannel $109 ($87; LinkedIn, SMS and voice-message automation, WhatsApp add-on, built-in dialer/VoIP). Add-ons: enrichment ($20 for 2K credits) and buying-intent signals ($29 for 100). lemAgent, previously AI Copilot and marked 'New', is a conversational layer that produces a campaign brief, a branching sequence and copy for each channel. The user reviews and launches it. lemlist says later campaigns draw on stored knowledge of the company, audiences and past results. Usage is metered per conversation with a daily workspace limit. The lemlist MCP server and CLI are included on paid plans. An industry tracker reports a native Claude Connector listing around 2026-07-26 (secondary).
findings.why_it_matters: This illustrates two patterns now common in outbound: conversational campaign building that persists memory across campaigns, and MCP access so external assistants can drive the tool. Operator AI's growth-operator workspace needs both, plus multichannel coverage (email, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, calls).

findings.title: Clay repriced on 2026-03-11: platform 'Actions' metered separately from 'Data Credits'; token-based pricing for frontier models
findings.detail: Third-party analyses agree that on 2026-03-11 Clay split usage into Data Credits (buying enrichment data, now 50–90% cheaper) and Actions (platform operations: each enrichment step, export and HTTP call). The old Starter $149 / Explorer $349 / Pro $800 plans were replaced by Free, Launch ($167 annual / $185 monthly; 15K actions, 3K credits), Growth ($446 / $495; 40K actions, 6K credits, CRM and warehouse sync, HTTP API/webhooks, web-intent signals) and Enterprise. Actions cannot be topped up, so running out means upgrading. Claygent (AI web researcher) and multi-provider waterfalls are on every plan, including Free. Signals (job change, company news, social listening) start at Launch. Clay's pricing page says token-heavy models (named GPT-5.1 and Claude 4.6 Sonnet) now carry variable, token-based pricing. The pricing page itself shows conflicting figures between its header and FAQ.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the reference for enrichment and research-agent economics. Students prospecting creator clients will use Clay-style waterfalls, and Operator AI's own research or enrichment agents need transparent usage metering because users now expect it.

findings.title: Mailbox-provider rules now enforced with rejections: Gmail/Yahoo (2024), Microsoft (May 2025), Gmail enforcement ramp-up (Nov 2025)
findings.detail: Senders above about 5,000 messages/day to consumer mailboxes must have SPF, DKIM and DMARC (at least p=none, aligned), RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe, and spam complaints below 0.3% (the Gmail/Yahoo benchmark). Microsoft began enforcing on 2025-05-05 for Outlook.com, Hotmail and Live: non-compliant mail goes first to Junk and may later be rejected. Google added a note on 2025-11-03 that enforcement was ramping up, with non-compliant traffic increasingly deferred (4xx) or rejected (5xx). Bulk-sender status is reported to be permanent once reached. These summaries come from deliverability vendors; the providers' own pages were not fetched.
findings.why_it_matters: This is why deliverability features (warmup, inbox rotation, IP sharding, placement tests) are table stakes in outbound tools. Operator AI's email and webinar follow-up must enforce authentication, unsubscribe and complaint thresholds for creator clients, or it will damage their domains.

findings.title: Gong's Revenue Harness (June 2026): natural-language Custom Agents with scoped access, audit trail and configurable human oversight, on usage-based Gong Credits
findings.detail: Gong's press release of 2026-06-24 introduced 'Mission Big Dipper' and the Gong Revenue Harness, an agentic layer that governs and connects AI agents across the revenue cycle. It builds on Agent Studio and MCP support; Gong's 2026-06-09 blog announced MCP, which was reported live around July 2026. Custom Agents, GA in June 2026, let RevOps leaders or managers describe a workflow in plain English (example: monitor $100K+ accounts for risk and alert the AE). They run with scoped data access, a full audit trail, configurable human oversight and the user's existing Gong permissions. Other named features: AI Builder for Scorecards, AI Trainer followed by AI Coach, and a standalone Gong Assistant workspace. Gong Credits (help doc updated 2026-10-20) meter heavier AI work: question-based AI trackers, API and MCP requests, deep mode, enrichment and automated briefs (10 credits per web search). Admins can set per-person or per-team caps and get 60–100% alerts. When credits run out, those features stop processing and API/MCP calls error. Seats are not publicly priced; third-party estimates are about $1,200–2,400 per seat per year plus platform fees.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the enterprise reference for 'governed agents': audit trail, scoped permissions, human oversight and budget caps. Operator AI's approval gating and role-based access should at least match this governance model, in a form a coaching business can operate.

findings.title: Sybill and Fathom: cheap call recording, summaries and CRM autofill; MCP is now available on low tiers, but often read-only
findings.detail: Fathom's pricing page (fetched 2026-10-27): Free (unlimited recording and transcription, instant summaries, limited Ask Fathom), Premium $20/mo ($16 annual), Team $19/user ($15), Business $34/user ($25; CRM field sync, Deal View, coaching metrics, AI scorecards, custom summaries), Enterprise custom. Fathom 3.0 (Product Hunt, 2026-04-15) added bot-free capture and ChatGPT/Claude support. An official MCP server on all plans is reported from around April 2026 (secondary source). Superhuman agreed to acquire Fathom (TechCrunch, 2026-09-14), citing more than 400K MAU and the goal of giving Superhuman's agents meeting context so they can draft follow-ups and update records. Sybill (third-party, checked 2026-10-06): Free, Pro $30 / Business $90 per user per month billed annually; the top plan was cut from $108 to $90 on 2026-10-11. CRM autofill (10 fields) and an MCP server start on Business. A competitor reports Sybill's MCP as read-only (ask, list and get conversations, deals and accounts, with no CRM writes) and Business AI credits capped at 5,000/week.
findings.why_it_matters: Call review is now nearly free. Value has moved to acting on calls: auto-filled CRM, drafted follow-ups and scorecards that feed coaching. Operator AI's closer and coach review should treat recording and transcripts as an input it gets from integrations, and compete on coaching and next actions.

findings.title: Table stakes in 2026 (in 5+ of the products reviewed): an MCP server, natural-language agent builders, auto-CRM fill, and usage credits on top of seats
findings.detail: (1) MCP server or connector: HighLevel (2025-07), Gong (2026-06/07), Kajabi, Circle (Business+), lemlist (+CLI), Fathom, Sybill (Business+). Smartlead and Clay offer API, webhooks and CLI. (2) Plain-language agent builders or operators: Gong Custom Agents, GHL Agent Studio, Smartlead SmartAgents, lemAgent, Instantly AI Sales Agent, Circle AI, Kajabi Cofounder, Hyperbound Kota Automations/Actions. (3) Automatic CRM updates and follow-up drafts from calls: Hyperbound Auto-CRM Fill and Deal Debrief, Sybill, Fathom Business, Gong. (4) Usage metering layered on subscriptions: Gong Credits, Clay Actions and Data Credits, Instantly credits, GHL pay-per-use and token-billed Agent Studio, Circle and Kajabi AI credits, Sybill weekly credits, lemAgent per-conversation limits. (5) Voice agents or voice calls: GHL Voice AI, Delphi, Utari, plus voice roleplay in Hyperbound and Second Nature. (6) Slack as an agent surface: Hyperbound Kota in Slack, Delphi Slack, Instantly Slack alerts. (7) Deliverability tooling in every outbound tool: warmup, rotation, placement tests.
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI needs these to be credible in 2026: an MCP and integration story, usage transparency with budget caps, auto-CRM and follow-up drafting, voice, and Slack or mobile notifications. Competing on any one of these alone will not differentiate it.

findings.title: Approval-gating is spreading but stays per-tool: drafts-only MCPs, review-before-launch and HITL modes; DM setters mostly lack it
findings.detail: Explicit human-approval patterns found: Kajabi MCP saves every write as a draft and turns sensitive scopes off by default. Circle AI proposes a setup that the operator approves before anything is built. Instantly's AI Sales Agent has a Human-in-the-loop mode. lemAgent builds a campaign the user reviews, then launches. Gong Custom Agents have configurable human oversight and an audit trail. HighLevel MCP uses scoped tokens. Meta Business Agent lets the business choose when a human takes over. By contrast, a vendor round-up of six Instagram/WhatsApp AI setters (SetSmart, Setter AI, Appointwise, CloseBot, InstantDM, Inrō) found none with a human-approval step. No product reviewed offers one approval and audit layer across multiple roles (owner/coach/setter/closer/student) and multiple tools.
findings.why_it_matters: This shows demand for Operator AI's core idea while leaving room to differentiate. Approval-gating is now normal UX, so it is not a differentiator in itself. A single, role-aware approval queue with an audit trail across ads, DMs, email, sales and fulfilment is something no reviewed product offers.

findings.title: Most differentiated capabilities seen across competitors
findings.detail: Standout capabilities that only one or a few products have: (a) An agentic clone that runs operations (ad accounts, CRM, reports) and takes voice calls: Utari (vendor claim, application-only). (b) A loop from practice to real calls to targeted re-practice, plus live in-call answers: Hyperbound (Real Call Scoring, Bitesized Roleplays from real-call signals, Live Call Coaching). (c) Generating a roleplay from an uploaded file, multi-persona sessions and video avatars: Second Nature. (d) A governed agent harness with audit trail and per-feature credit caps: Gong. (e) Free distribution of a native DM agent inside the platform: Meta Business Agent. (f) Deliverability at infrastructure level (server/IP sharding and rotation): Instantly SISR. (g) Campaign memory that improves later campaigns: lemAgent (vendor claim). (h) Daily operator brief with recommendations plus AI-built paywalls: Circle AI. (i) A digital mind with citations and turning corrections into Q&A: Delphi.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the feature bar for each of Operator AI's surfaces. A combination none of these vendors offers is clone, setter, closer training, call review and fulfilment ops in one approval-gated, white-label workspace built for the growth-operator business model.

findings.title: Consolidation and platform risk: notetakers being absorbed, platforms shipping native agents, add-ons being retired
findings.detail: Recent signals: Superhuman agreed to acquire Fathom (2026-09-14) to feed meeting context to its agents. Meta launched a free native Business Agent across WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger (2026-06-03). Kajabi's Creator Studio add-on is reported to close on 2026-11-09 while Kajabi pushes Cofounder, MCP and Expert Agents. Circle and Kajabi now build communities, paywalls and pages with AI. Hyperbound was named in Gartner's first Market Overview for B2B sales AI roleplay (Aug 2026), a sign the category is maturing. Third-party tools that depend on another platform's API (setters on GHL or Meta, notetakers) are being squeezed or bought.
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI should build on stable integration surfaces (MCP, official APIs) and own the layers platforms are unlikely to build: role-based approval, the programme and curriculum layer for students, and cross-tool attribution. Native platform features will keep commoditising single-function bots.

findings.title: What a growth operator actually does: runs the creator's back end while the creator supplies the audience
findings.detail: Explainers and reviews describe the same scope. The operator runs the behind-the-scenes side of a creator's or expert's info-product business. That covers choosing and building the offer (often a low-ticket lead magnet or ebook that leads into high-ticket coaching, or a paid community on Skool, Whop or Discord), building funnels, emails, automations and tracking, handling lead follow-up and sales, and adding paid ads (Meta first) on top of the creator's organic audience. Whop's own explainer says the model is not new and has simply been renamed. A critical October 2026 review describes the current pitch as auditing a selling educator's sales pages, funnels and follow-up, then improving lead capture, follow-up speed, call scoring and tracking (often with AI tools) for a share of profits. Practitioners say the hard parts are landing the first creator without case studies, and fulfilment once a creator signs. Little public material covers fulfilment.
findings.why_it_matters: This defines the core objects Operator AI must model: creator client, offer ladder, funnel, community or product, ad account, sales team and tracking. It also points to a real gap, because training covers 'land a creator' well and 'run the back end' poorly. The approval-gated OS can fill that gap.

sources.publisher: Ippei.com (review site that sells a competing program)

findings.title: Deal structures: profit or revenue share of 10-30%, hybrid retainer plus share, and big setup fees for done-for-you work
findings.detail: Reported growth-operator terms are 10-30% of profits, set contract by contract (critical review, Oct 2026). Secondary coverage of one large programme's pitch cites 30% of revenue. Agency-pricing guides for 2026 describe the hybrid as a base retainer plus a percentage of incremental revenue above a baseline. One worked example takes 20% of incremental revenue. Other guides suggest 5-10% for established businesses and 15-25% for startups, or 4-8% of additional revenue for coaches and consultants. The guides warn that 'incremental' is hard to attribute and often disputed. Retainers are reportedly the main model for 78% of agencies (a cited 2026 survey). Done-for-you acquisition agencies that serve coaches state a $12,500 minimum investment with ad spend billed separately (Scaling With Systems), or a 3-month contract (Konvert). Reviewers note that rev-share income is volatile and that operators often carry tool costs (estimated at $500-$5,000 a month for AI agencies).
findings.why_it_matters: Rev-share payouts need an agreed baseline, an agreed attribution source and a reconciliation ledger: gross vs net, refunds, platform fees, and who pays ad spend. Disputes over 'incremental' revenue are a predictable cause of churn, so a deal-terms record plus monthly settlement statements is a clear job for the product.

findings.title: Choosing a niche and finding creator clients: target creators who already sell, judge fit over follower count, and expect outreach to be the bottleneck
findings.detail: Whop suggests targeting 'make money online' coaches (ecommerce, copywriting, web design), because their audiences already buy. It suggests finding creators organically on Instagram, YouTube and TikTok or with discovery tools. Reviews of 2026 programmes say they target educators who already sell courses or mentorships. General creator-outreach guides add these steps: write an ideal-partner profile (follower range, minimum engagement, niche, audience, brand safety); check account health (overnight follower spikes, engagement drops, fake followers); open with something specific from the creator's recent content; follow up only once or twice; and track a pipeline of prospect, contacted, replied, negotiating, active and not a fit. Reply rates are vendor anecdotes only: about 5-10% for cold outreach, and claims of 50% or more when the operator comments on the creator's posts before messaging. I found no credible public benchmark for how many DMs or touches it takes to sign a growth-operator client, or for the close rate on those partnership calls.
findings.why_it_matters: Students need a prospect-research and qualification workspace: an ICP scorecard, account-health checks, personalised opener drafts that need approval before sending, a follow-up cap and a pipeline. The lack of public conversion data means Operator AI's own aggregated, anonymised funnel data could become a differentiator.

findings.title: Cold Instagram DM outreach has no published cap; limits are trust-based and action blocks are a real operational risk
findings.detail: Third-party 2026 guides agree that Meta publishes no daily DM limit for manual messages. Their estimates for messages to non-followers vary widely: 10-20 a day for new accounts, 30-50 for accounts aged 3-12 months, and 50-100 for established accounts. Cold DMs land in message requests, which many users never open. Reported action blocks last from a few hours to 5 days and get longer for repeat offences. Tools quote figures such as '200 automated DMs an hour', but these are the tools' own pacing choices, not Meta rules.
findings.why_it_matters: Outreach agents and setters working from client or student Instagram accounts need per-account pacing, warm-up by account age, block detection and human-sent messages for cold outreach. Bulk automated cold DMs put the creator's main asset, their account, at risk.

findings.title: Meta messaging policy constrains automated DM setting: 24-hour window, a manual-only 7-day Human Agent tag, bot disclosure and 30-second bot replies
findings.detail: Meta's Messenger Platform and IG Messaging API policy works as follows. Businesses may reply during a standard window, usually 24 hours after the user's last message, and those replies may be promotional. After a user's first message from a Click-to-Messenger or Click-to-Direct ad, the window can last up to 7 days. The Human Agent tag allows a person to reply manually for 7 days. Third-party guides say it needs its own app review and must not be used by automation. Tags cannot carry promotional content. One-time notifications, news messaging and Sponsored Messages are not available on Instagram. Where the law requires it, automated chats must say they are a bot at the start of a conversation, after a long gap and when switching from a human to automation (California and Germany are called out). Bots must respond to input within 30 seconds. Comment-triggered private replies follow separate rules (one private reply within 7 days, per vendor guides). Meta docs cited in search results list some Messenger message tags (confirmed event update, account update, post-purchase update) as removed from 10 Feb 2026. A further tag change reported for 27 Apr 2026 is unverified.
findings.why_it_matters: Every DM-setting automation in Operator AI needs these rules built in: window timers, a manual-only path for the Human Agent tag, no promotions in tags, bot-disclosure text and response-time monitoring. Click-to-Direct ads are the compliant way to get a 7-day automated window.

findings.title: EU AI Act Article 50 chatbot-disclosure duties applied from 2 Aug 2026 and were not delayed by the Digital Omnibus
findings.detail: From 2 August 2026, systems that interact with people must make clear that the user is dealing with AI, unless that is already obvious. Deployers must label deepfake image, audio or video. AI-generated text published on matters of public interest must be disclosed unless it has had human editorial review. The Digital Omnibus moved Annex III high-risk deadlines to 2 Dec 2027 (and Annex I to 2 Aug 2028), but most Article 50 duties went ahead. The only extension is for machine-readable marking (Art. 50(2)), which gives generative systems already on the market until 2 Dec 2026. Fines can reach EUR 15M or 3% of worldwide turnover. Commentators say Omnibus publication dates still needed confirmation in the Official Journal.
findings.why_it_matters: AI setters, AI DM replies and AI-generated ad creative (for example, cloned creator voice or face) aimed at EU prospects need disclosure and labelling. Operator AI's approval gate is a natural place to enforce disclosure templates and labelling of synthetic media.

findings.title: US TCPA 'revoke-all' consent rule pushed back to 31 Jan 2027, and may still change
findings.detail: FCC Order DA-26-12A (6 Jan 2026) moved the effective date of 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10) from 11 Apr 2026 to 31 Jan 2027. This is the second delay. Under the rule, a consumer opting out of one automated call or text would opt them out of all future automated calls and texts from that caller, including on unrelated topics. A further notice of proposed rulemaking suggests the FCC may soften this 'stop one, stop all' approach before it takes effect. The sources do not settle how it applies to appointment reminders.
findings.why_it_matters: Pre-call SMS reminder sequences, dialer campaigns and re-engagement texts to US leads all need a cross-channel opt-out registry ready before Jan 2027. A single consent ledger across SMS, voice and DM is a compliance feature buyers will understand.

findings.title: FTC keeps acting against earnings, growth and refund-guarantee claims in coaching and business-opportunity sales
findings.detail: In March 2026 the FTC filed a proposed order against Air AI and its owners. It bans them from marketing business opportunities, requires substantiation and disclosure for any earnings claims, prohibits misrepresentations in telemarketing, and imposes an $18M judgment that is mostly suspended. The complaint alleged unsupported income claims, refund and buy-back guarantees that were not honoured, and violations of the Business Opportunity Rule and the Telemarketing Sales Rule (TSR). Earlier, in June 2025, an order permanently banned Ascend Ecom from selling business opportunities or coaching. A January 2025 FTC proposal would extend the Business Opportunity Rule to 'money-making opportunities', including business coaching and online courses. It drew dissents, its status in 2026 is unclear, and I could not confirm a final rule.
findings.why_it_matters: This affects the programme (students are sold an income opportunity) and many creator clients (often in make-money niches). Operator AI should gate income and result claims in ads, VSLs, DM scripts and sales calls behind approval, store substantiation for testimonials, and record refund and guarantee terms and whether they were honoured.
