verify.area: Rules and compliance: Meta, WhatsApp and LinkedIn messaging; Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook email; CAN-SPAM; TCPA, 10DLC and state texting law; UK and EU privacy; FTC reviews and earnings claims; ROSCA; EU AI Act and US AI disclosure and likeness laws

checks.title: Meta Messenger/IG 24h window, Human Agent tag, three utility tags removed 2026-04-27
checks.evidence: There is no Meta Send API sender. queue.py:49 MANUAL_CHANNELS covers instagram_dm, facebook_dm and whatsapp. These items always go to awaiting_manual_send (delivery.manual_reason): a named person sends them and confirms. queue.mark_sent (queue.py:527-544) audits the confirmation as confirmed_by. live/senders.py has no Meta channel. Webinar reminders and booking confirmations go by email or calendar (webinars._create_send, live/chain.pick_slot), never by message tags. Playbooks already describe the window, the Human Agent tag and the removed tags (content-organic-email instagram-comment-to-dm-messaging-rules; growth-operator-model social-dm-automation-limits).
checks.gap: Only matters if a Meta API sender is ever added. It would then need a window clock per thread (24h, or 7 days for ad-originated threads), a hard block after expiry, and Human Agent use only for messages a person typed.

checks.title: Instagram comment-to-DM private replies: one per commenter, 7 days, follow-ups only after a reply
checks.evidence: The code has no comment-trigger or private-reply feature (grep finds no private_repl or instagram_manage). Cold IG prospecting is human-sent: prospects.CHANNELS instagram_dm goes to awaiting_manual_send, DEFAULT_CAPS allows 20 DMs a day, and the daily_cap guard applies. The playbooks cover the rules (instagram-comment-to-dm-messaging-rules, instagram-messaging-rate-limits at 750 an hour, comment-keyword-dm-funnel-design).
checks.gap: If a comment-trigger builder is built, it must allow one opener per commenter, drop comments older than 7 days, send no drip before a reply, and pace under the rate limit. Guardrails do not catch 'follow/like to get the link' gating today.

checks.title: Meta automated-chat requirements: human escalation path and bot disclosure
checks.evidence: No automated chat runs on Meta: every IG/FB reply is drafted for approval and sent by a person (inbound.py docstring steps 3-7; departments._instructions says 'Everything you write goes to the approval queue'). Human escalation does exist: legal threats, refunds and complaints go to escalations.raise_ (OWNER_RESOLVES), and unknown senders get a needs_human holding draft.
checks.gap: Becomes binding only with a Meta API agent, which would need an always-on 'talk to a human' handoff, a disclosure at start and on bot takeover, and the 30-day Requests staleness rule. The general AI disclosure gap on the public minis and the phone line is covered under the state bot-disclosure check.

checks.title: WhatsApp Business terms bar general-purpose AI assistants from 15 Jan 2026
checks.evidence: whatsapp appears only as a manual channel (queue.MANUAL_CHANNELS, delivery.CHANNEL_LABEL). There is no WhatsApp Business API integration and no WhatsApp bot.
checks.gap: No playbook entry mentions the WhatsApp AI-provider terms (grep of the playbooks finds nothing). If a WhatsApp agent is added, it needs a stored per-tenant scope (qualification, booking, FAQ) and a topic guardrail.

checks.title: LinkedIn User Agreement bans automation and scraping
checks.evidence: linkedin is in queue.MANUAL_CHANNELS, so messages are always copy-and-send by a human who then confirms 'I sent it'. The code has no LinkedIn API, scraper or extension. Prospect web research reads only the prospect's own site, behind a server switch, and respects robots.txt (prospects.py docstring). The linkedin-outreach-limits-and-practice and agentic-outreach-guardrails playbooks cite the 3 Nov 2025 agreement.
checks.gap: CSV import from 'any lead tool' (prospects.import_csv) never asks whether the data is LinkedIn-scraped enrichment; it requires only a free-text lawful note. There is no LinkedIn volume coaching: prospects.CHANNELS covers only instagram_dm and email, so LinkedIn sends are not counted toward any cap.

checks.title: Gmail sender rules: stricter enforcement since Nov 2025
checks.evidence: Live prospect emails get List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post one-click headers plus a body link (delivery.send_live, senders.EMAIL_HEADERS). /u/{token} unsubscribes immediately (delivery.unsubscribe). Each ARF spam complaint puts that recipient on do-not-contact (channels._bounce_of then inbound.apply_dnc). SMTP sending uses STARTTLS. A new mailbox warms up (DEFAULT_SETTINGS: 40 a day, starting at 10 and adding 5 a day). Prospect email is blocked until OPERATOR_PUBLIC_URL is set.
checks.gap: Nothing checks SPF, DKIM, DMARC alignment or PTR before sending (grep of operator_ai/ and scripts/ finds nothing; preflight_live.py checks only vault fields). Nothing reads Postmaster spam rate, warns at 0.1% or pauses at 0.3%. Webinar emails (webinars._create_send, client_asset mode) carry only a body link: send_live adds the one-click headers only when _is_prospect_email.

checks.title: Yahoo bulk-sender rules: DMARC, RFC 8058, unsubscribes within 2 days, complaints under 0.3%
checks.evidence: Unsubscribes and STOP replies are applied at once (delivery.unsubscribe, inbound.apply_dnc), well inside 2 days. Prospect emails carry the one-click headers.
checks.gap: Same gaps as Gmail: no authentication preflight, no complaint-rate monitoring, and no one-click headers on webinar or other marketing email. Yahoo sets no volume threshold, so these apply at any volume.

checks.title: Microsoft Outlook.com high-volume rules; failures bounce with 550 5.7.515
checks.evidence: A synchronous SMTP rejection in live/senders.send becomes a generic SendError and then a 502 'Try again', with no domain-level stop. Worse, channels._bounce_of treats any DSN with Status 5.x as a recipient hard bounce, and inbound.apply_dnc then puts that recipient on permanent do-not-contact.
checks.gap: Today a 5.7.515 (or Gmail 5.7.26) sender-authentication failure would wrongly put every affected recipient on do-not-contact while other sends continue. The 5.7.x authentication and policy codes should be classed as sender-side: pause the domain and open a DNS-fix task for the owner.

checks.title: CAN-SPAM covers B2B cold email; $53,088 per email; sender and seller both liable
checks.evidence: delivery.with_footer adds the real sender's name, postal address and an unsubscribe link. For a student's own outreach, delivery.sender_identity names the student as sender. guard_rules blocks missing_postal_address and missing_unsubscribe. The deceptive_subject rule blocks a 'Re:' or 'Fwd:' subject on a first touch. The suppressions table is tenant-wide, and unsubscribe tokens keep working.
checks.gap: Cold prospect emails never say they are an advertisement or solicitation (grep for 'advertis' in delivery and guardrails finds nothing). Webinar emails, including the post-event sales sequence, carry no postal address: webinars.with_unsubscribe adds only the unsubscribe line, and client_asset mode skips the footer guard. There is no record that a creator client approved mail sent in its name across tenants.

checks.title: TCPA revocation: any reasonable means, 10 business days, Sept 2026 exclusive-method order, revoke-all waived to 2027-01-31
checks.evidence: inbound.opt_keyword recognises STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT, OPTOUT and REVOKE, plus free-text phrasings (_OPT_OUT_PHRASE). inbound.apply_dnc acts at once: do_not_contact on the prospect or lead (which queue._check then blocks on every channel), the never-contact list, delivery suppression, held queue items, and opt-out of both sms and phone.
checks.gap: SMS bodies never carry 'Reply STOP to opt out': STOP_LINE and EMAIL_FOOTER are added to email only (missions/registry.py:902/967, inbound.py:957). Informational streams such as programme reminders are not separated from marketing. A student's or member's SMS STOP updates only that channel_link, not other channels. No single non-marketing confirmation text is sent.

checks.title: AI-generated voices are 'artificial' under the TCPA
checks.evidence: No outbound AI voice exists. channels.voice_call is inbound only, answers only opted-in callers, and uses the constant NEUTRAL_TTS_VOICES. Outbound 'phone' items are manual (a human dials) and are blocked by not_opted_in without opt-in (queue._check).
checks.gap: The inbound line greets callers with 'Hi, ask me anything about the programme.' It does not name the business or say it is automated.

checks.title: One-to-one consent rule vacated; written consent must still be provable per seller
checks.evidence: SMS and phone sends require opt-in (queue._check not_opted_in). Opt-ins are stored in channel_links or contact_points with a timestamp and source. An opt-in the owner records from outside the app is audited as consent. Webinar registration needs a ticked consent box and audits consent with its source (webinars.register).
checks.gap: No prior express written consent record is kept: no seller name, no snapshot of the disclosure text, no IP, user agent or form version. webinar_registrants stores only consent=1; the IP is used for rate limiting and then dropped. No opt-in form captures SMS or AI-voice consent, and consent proof cannot be exported per client.

checks.title: TCPA quiet hours: 8am to 9pm recipient local time
checks.evidence: Nothing resolves a recipient's time zone or area code, and there is no send window (grep for quiet hours or area code finds nothing). delivery.next_morning uses server local time. dispatch_due sends scheduled items, cadence follow-ups included, whenever they fall due. live/senders.send sends SMS with no time check.
checks.gap: Need recipient time-zone resolution, a conservative window such as 9am to 8pm local, and queueing outside it, for SMS and voice items that dispatch automatically.

checks.title: Texas SB 140: marketing texts under telemarketing law with a private right of action
checks.evidence: Every sms or phone item without opt-in is blocked in every state (queue._check not_opted_in). STOP is honoured immediately.
checks.gap: No consent provenance is kept per message (see the consent-proof check). The playbook state-mini-tcpa-florida-texas still tells users to confirm Chapter 302 registration and has not caught up with the Texas AG's November 2025 clarification.

checks.title: US A2P 10DLC: unregistered traffic blocked since Feb 2025
checks.evidence: live/senders.ready checks only live_channels_enabled and the vault fields sms_account_sid, sms_auth_token and sms_from_number. Nothing stores brand or campaign registration, gates on it, matches use case to content, or handles carrier error codes. The playbook a2p-10dlc-registration describes it all.
checks.gap: Need per-tenant brand and campaign registration status as a send gate, opt-out language in sample messages, use-case and content matching, and an automatic pause on carrier filtering errors.

checks.title: UK PECR and UK GDPR B2B: corporate vs sole trader; PECR fines now £17.5m or 4%
checks.evidence: Every import or manual add needs a lawful basis and a note (prospects._check_basis, LAWFUL_BASES). Do-not-contact is permanent, and the suppression list is tenant-wide.

findings.title: Meta Andromeda made creative diversity, not audience targeting, the main lever for who sees an ad
findings.detail: Andromeda is Meta's ad-retrieval stage. Meta's engineering team described it in Dec 2024. It cuts tens of millions of eligible ads down to a few thousand candidates before ranking. In an April 22, 2025 business post, Meta said creative diversification is now the best way to find relevant audiences, and that narrow demographic or interest targeting matters less. Meta claims Andromeda improved ads quality by 8%. Meta did not set a number of creatives to aim for. Its example of an advertiser going from 3-4 to about 50 new creatives a week is a testimonial, not guidance. Practitioner Jon Loomer (published Aug 19, 2025, updated Dec 15, 2025) reports that Meta dropped its old advice of no more than 6 ads per ad set. He recommends broad ad sets in which ads differ in concept, angle, format and persona, rather than copy tweaks. All performance figures here are Meta's own claims.
findings.why_it_matters: For a growth operator, targeting work now becomes creative work: many distinct angles (pain, proof, demo, identity, objection) for each creator offer. Operator AI's ad workflow should plan and track concept diversity and route each new batch for approval. It should not spend effort on interest-stack audiences.

findings.title: Practitioners say near-duplicate creatives get grouped and compete as one ad (not confirmed by Meta)
findings.detail: Several 2025-2026 agency and tool-vendor posts say Andromeda groups ads that look or sound alike (visuals, copy, audio) under one shared identifier, often called an 'entity ID'. On that model, 30-50 small variants behave like one ad in retrieval. One vendor says 'entity ID' is industry shorthand, not a Meta term. Some posts give specific 'creative similarity score' cut-offs (40% or 60%) and claim more ROAS for accounts testing 20+ ads. I found no Meta document behind any of these numbers. Vendor posts also say creative lifespans shrank to about 2-3 weeks after Andromeda; that is also unverified.
findings.why_it_matters: If this model is right, counting variants overstates real testing. Operator AI could score how similar new creatives are to each other (hook, format, persona, setting) and flag cosmetic variants before they go for approval. The specific thresholds should not be presented as platform rules.

findings.title: Creative volume norms: large Meta dataset shows about 5% of creatives become 'winners'; more volume gives more chances, not better odds per ad
findings.detail: Motion's Creative Benchmarks 2026 (page updated Apr 17, 2026) covers $1.29B of Meta spend, 578,750 creatives and 6,015 advertiser accounts, Sep 1 2025 to Jan 1 2026. A 'winner' is a creative that spends at least 10x the account median and at least $500. The overall hit rate is about 5%; the page also says about 7.7% clear the 10x threshold and does not reconcile the two. Enterprise accounts launched about 18.8 new creatives a week. Winners took 23% of spend in micro accounts and 64% in enterprise accounts. Motion's view is that volume adds chances to find a winner but does not change the odds for any single creative. The study measures spend share only, not ROAS or conversions, and has no coaching or info-product breakdown. Vendor rules of thumb for weekly volume differ about tenfold, e.g. 3-5 a week at $5-15k a month versus 20-30 a week per $100k a month.
findings.why_it_matters: This gives a defensible planning number (about 1 in 20 creatives becomes a spend winner) for setting creative-production targets with creator clients. Operator AI can use it to size creative requests to the budget and to explain to students why most tests 'fail'.

findings.title: Advantage+ is now on by default for Sales, App and Leads campaigns, and the default audience cannot set age or gender limits
findings.detail: In early 2025 Meta replaced the manual-versus-automated choice. Advantage+ (Audience, Placements and Budget) is now on by default for Sales, App and Leads objectives, and Advantage+ Shopping became Advantage+ Sales. Changing some settings, such as making age, gender or custom-audience suggestions strict, turns Advantage+ off. Meta claims about 9% lower CPA for Advantage+ sales campaigns. In early tests Meta also claimed about 10% lower cost per qualified lead for leads campaigns with Advantage+ on; Loomer questions whether that reflects real lead quality. Advantage+ Audience cannot set age or gender limits, which practitioners say can hurt lead quality for high-ticket offers.
findings.why_it_matters: High-ticket coaching depends on qualified, solvent leads. Operator AI should help students choose between full Advantage+ and constrained setups, and judge results on CRM-qualified leads and booked calls, not form fills.

findings.title: Meta targeting in 2026: detailed targeting and lookalikes are mostly 'suggestions'; the remaining hard controls are location, minimum age and custom-audience exclusions
findings.detail: Loomer's March 24, 2026 review of targeting: with Advantage+ on by default, detailed targeting is only a suggestion and cannot be made strict for 11 common performance goals; lookalikes cannot be made strict for 9. Hard controls that remain are location, a minimum age between 18 and 25, and custom-audience exclusions, which still let some excluded people through. Detailed-targeting exclusions were removed for new campaigns in 2024; a 2026 guide says they were removed from active campaigns on March 31, 2025. Account-level audience controls (locations, minimum age, exclusions) apply to every campaign in the account.
findings.why_it_matters: Most of the 'targeting' a student once configured is gone. Operator AI's ad-setup checks should cover account-level controls (geo, age, exclusions of existing clients and students) and steer qualification into creative copy and the funnel (application questions).

findings.title: Meta is testing removal of ad-set-level placement exclusions for Sales and Leads; control moves to account-level settings and value rules
findings.detail: Reports from Aug 20, 2026 describe an in-product Ads Manager notice saying ad-set-level exclusions of placements and platforms (some reports add devices and operating systems) would no longer be available. Jon Loomer first spotted it. As of early Sep 2026 it was a rolling test tied to Sales and Leads objectives, with sensitive verticals excluded, and Meta had published no announcement. What remains: account-level placement controls (availability varies) and value rules, which adjust bid preference by placement from +1000% to -90% but cannot block a placement. Meta's documentation claims Advantage+ placements give an average 11.7% lower cost per action than manual placements.
findings.why_it_matters: Coaches often exclude Audience Network or low-intent placements to protect lead quality. Operator AI should flag where account-level controls are the only exclusion left and watch lead quality by placement.

findings.title: Meta attribution rewritten in 2025-2026: view windows removed from the API, click-through now means link clicks only, and 'engage-through' added
findings.detail: Meta announced in Oct 2025 that from Jan 12, 2026 the Ads Insights API would stop returning 7-day view and 28-day view windows in all API versions. It also limited unique-count breakdowns to 13 months and frequency breakdowns to 6 months of history. In March 2026, Meta changed click-through attribution to count only conversions after a link click. A new 'engage-through' window replaced engaged-view and covers social clicks, likes, shares, saves and 5-second video views. The default is now 7-day click, 1-day engage-through, 1-day view. 28-day click can be viewed in reports but not used for optimisation. Meta says billing did not change, but reported click-through conversions fall. Meta also claims that Incremental Attribution, launched in 2025, drove 24% more incremental conversions than standard attribution in Q4 2025 (Meta claim).
findings.why_it_matters: Any dashboard comparing results before and after March 2026 will show artificial drops. Operator AI's reporting should label attribution settings and use the CRM (booked, showed, closed) as the source of truth instead of Ads Manager ROAS.

findings.title: Signal quality: Meta can optimise for CRM sales stages (booked, showed, closed) if lead stages are sent back through Conversions API for CRM
findings.detail: Meta's developer documentation for Conversion Leads optimisation lists these fit criteria: Lead Ads (Instant Forms) only; at least 200 leads a month; data uploaded at least daily; the target stage happens within 28 days of the lead; and the target stage converts 1-40% of leads. Meta recommends storing its 15-17 digit Lead ID in the CRM and sending it with each stage event; email, phone or click ID are fallbacks. Meta expects about 1 month before results show. Meta's CAPI best practices say only matched events are used for attribution and optimisation, scored by Event Match Quality out of 10; Meta publishes no target score. An agency study (Focus Digital, 2026) claims CAPI users see 15-25% lower CPL, but its baseline is inconsistent; treat that as unverified.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a core Operator AI workflow. The setter/closer pipeline (qualified, booked, showed, closed) can be sent to Meta so ads optimise for calls that show and close, not cheap form fills. Every stage write should be approval-gated and auditable. Website, VSL or webinar funnels need a separate custom-event CAPI path, because Conversion Leads works only with Instant Forms.

findings.title: Health and wellness coaches face restricted conversion signals on Meta (since about Jan-Feb 2025)
findings.detail: Several vendor and trade sources report that from about January-February 2025, Meta stopped accounts classified as health and wellness from sending lower-funnel standard events (Purchase, Lead, checkout) and from building custom audiences on blocked events. Under the most severe tier, all events can be blocked in some regions. The category is shown in Events Manager data-source settings. Vendors suggest renamed custom events sent through CAPI as a workaround; that may conflict with the intent of the policy. I did not retrieve a primary Meta policy page, so dates and tier definitions are unconfirmed.
findings.why_it_matters: Many creator clients in a growth-operator programme are fitness, nutrition or mindset coaches. Operator AI should check the dataset category during client onboarding, warn that optimisation may be limited, and not automatically recommend signal workarounds without human and compliance approval.

findings.title: Meta automatically labels AI-generated or AI-edited ads, including third-party tools detected through C2PA metadata (July 2026 update)
findings.detail: Social Media Today (Jul 7, 2026) reports that Meta updated its ad disclosures. Ads created or significantly edited with Meta's generative tools (Background Generation, Image Generation, Add Animation) get an 'AI info' disclosure in the 'About this ad' menu. So do ads Meta detects were made with third-party AI tools, using industry signals such as C2PA. The policy lives in Meta's Business Help Center ('About AI info on ads...'); I could not render the page text. Some vendor blogs claim 'undisclosed AI content' is now 14% of all ad rejections and describe a strike ladder; neither is in Meta's documentation, so treat both as unverified.
findings.why_it_matters: Students increasingly use AI avatars, voice clones and generated B-roll for creator clients. Operator AI should record which AI tools touched each asset, keep C2PA metadata, and warn when photorealistic synthetic people appear in testimonial-style ads.

findings.title: TikTok reportedly requires an AI disclosure label on ads with realistic AI content (effective Jul 21, 2026); Google mandates disclosure only for election ads
findings.detail: A UK agency (Aug 12, 2026) reports that from Jul 21, 2026 TikTok requires an ad-level 'AI disclosure' tag before an ad can run if it contains realistic AI elements: cloned or synthetic voiceovers, AI avatars or spokespeople, AI-edited visuals, or photorealistic AI imagery. Clearly stylised animation is outside the rule. Detection is reported to run whether or not an ad is tagged, with tiered penalties up to a permanent ban. TikTok adopted C2PA Content Credentials for auto-labelling in Jan 2025. I found no TikTok primary policy page to confirm the ad mandate. For Google, synthetic-content disclosure is clearly mandatory only for election ads (since 2023); claims about a global commercial-ad AI indicator are unconfirmed.
findings.why_it_matters: AI-avatar VSLs and voice-cloned ads are common in coaching. A cross-platform disclosure checklist in Operator AI's ad-approval step would cut rejection and account risk.

findings.title: 'Make money' and income-opportunity ads face Meta income-claim rules, review of the full ad unit, and a scam-ad pricing penalty
findings.detail: Meta's ad standards on unrealistic outcomes (Transparency Center; the page returned 404 when fetched, content seen in search results) ban promises that people can get rich quickly or with little work. Ads for income opportunities must fully describe the business model. Agency guides add that Meta reviews the landing page as part of the ad, and that openers implying a viewer's finances ('struggling coach?') are flagged under the personal-attributes rule. Reuters reported in Nov 2025, citing internal Meta documents, that Meta projected about 10% of 2024 revenue (about $16B) from scam and banned-goods ads. Per that report, Meta bans an advertiser only when its systems are 95% sure of fraud, and charges suspected-but-unconfirmed advertisers higher ad prices as a penalty. Meta called the estimate overly inclusive.
findings.why_it_matters: A programme teaching people to become 'growth operators' sells an income opportunity, and its creator clients often sell business or 'make money' coaching. Both sit near flagged categories. Operator AI should run claim and personal-attribute checks on ads and landing pages before approval, and watch for unexplained CPM inflation as a possible penalty signal.

findings.title: FTC keeps pursuing business-opportunity and coaching earnings claims, and has proposed bringing business coaching under the Business Opportunity Rule
findings.detail: On Jan 13, 2025 the FTC sought comment on expanding the Business Opportunity Rule to 'money-making opportunities' explicitly including business coaching, plus a separate Earnings Claim Rule aimed at MLMs. I found no final rule as of Oct 2026. The current rule (16 CFR 437) already requires a reasonable basis and written substantiation for earnings claims. Enforcement through 2025-2026 includes: a permanent ban for the operator of the 'AI-powered' FBA Machine storefront scheme (Jul 30, 2025); a court halt of the Click Profit scheme; a preliminary injunction against IM Mastery Academy (Aug 21, 2025); the Air AI suit (Aug 25, 2025); and an April 2026 proposed settlement with an MLM recruiter-coach over baseless earnings claims.
findings.why_it_matters: Earnings and 'replace your job' claims run through growth-operator recruiting and creator offers. Operator AI should require substantiation (typical results, sample) before approving any income or results claim in ads, VSLs, webinars or DM scripts, and keep an audit trail.

findings.title: AI sales-agent claims vs evidence: FTC sued an 'AI agent' seller over capability and earnings claims, and Gartner expects over 40% of agentic projects to be cancelled
findings.detail: The FTC sued Air AI (Aug 25, 2025, D. Ariz., 3-0 vote) under the Telemarketing Sales Rule and the Business Opportunity Rule. It alleges the company sold 'conversational AI' as a replacement for human reps that was unavailable or faulty for some buyers, made earnings claims, and offered refund guarantees (2-3x return) it rarely honoured. Some buyers lost up to $250,000. Coverage reports a later settlement barring Air AI from marketing business opportunities. Separately, Gartner (Jun 25, 2025) predicts that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end-2027 because of cost, unclear value or weak risk controls. Gartner also warns of 'agent washing' and estimates only about 130 of thousands of 'agentic' vendors are real.
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI is itself an agentic product sold into a coaching programme. Its own marketing, and any AI-setter performance claims students repeat to creator clients, need substantiation. Its approval gates and audit logs can be positioned as the risk controls Gartner says are missing.

findings.title: AI DM-setter tools for coaches publish large but unaudited performance claims
findings.detail: SetSmart is an AI setter for Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger aimed at fitness and business coaches. It qualifies leads on goals, budget and readiness and books calls; it does not close. It claims (vendor claim) a 2026 study of 828,000 DM conversations across 391 businesses: AI qualified 22.9% of engaged leads and 44.7% of those booked; another page says 1.94% of conversations booked, with denominators undefined. It also claims +106% booked calls from two automatic follow-ups (at 4h and 23h), and 'Official Meta Business Partner' status. Pricing is $25, $97 and $297 a month. The page does not mention AI disclosure to leads. Wider AI-SDR claims are also weak: a widely repeated '50-70% churn within a year' figure is unsourced. A Deloitte Digital study (Feb 2026, n=1,060 B2B suppliers and buyers, reported second-hand) found 45% of suppliers use AI in sales but only 24% have tried agentic AI.
findings.why_it_matters: The direct competitor set for Operator AI's setter role sells on headline booking lifts with no independent evidence. Operator AI can differentiate with transparent, per-tenant measurement (qualification, booked and show rates against a human-setter baseline) and human approval before sensitive messages.

findings.title: Meta is building its own AI sales agents ('Business AI') and pushing click-to-message ads, with fully automated ad creation as its stated aim
findings.detail: Meta's Jan 28, 2026 newsroom post reports these Q4 2025 figures (Meta claims): US click-to-message ad revenue up more than 50% year on year, led by Website-to-Message ads; WhatsApp paid messaging at a $2B annual run-rate; video-generation ad tools at a $10B combined run-rate; and Business AIs at over 1M weekly conversations in Mexico and the Philippines, with expansion to more markets planned in 2026. Meta also began testing an AI business assistant for advertisers in Q4 2025. In Oct 2025 Meta described Business AI as a sales concierge appearing on ads and websites. The WSJ reported in June 2025 that Meta aims to let advertisers supply only a product image and budget, with AI producing creative, targeting and budget by end-2026; I found no confirmation that this has shipped.
findings.why_it_matters: Native Meta AI agents answering ad-driven DMs could replace parts of the setter role for free. Operator AI's value then shifts to cross-channel orchestration, CRM truth, approvals, and coaching students on how to supervise platform AI.

findings.title: WhatsApp Business API has banned general-purpose AI chatbots since Jan 15, 2026; business-specific sales and booking bots are still allowed
findings.detail: Meta added an 'AI providers' section to the WhatsApp Business terms. It applied to new users from Oct 15, 2025 and to existing users from Jan 15, 2026, and bars distributing general-purpose AI assistants (e.g. ChatGPT, Perplexity) through the Business API. Meta said businesses using AI for customer service, bookings and similar purposes are unaffected. Meta keeps discretion to decide what counts as a bot's primary use.
findings.why_it_matters: An AI setter on WhatsApp must stay clearly scoped to the creator's own qualification and booking flow. An open-ended assistant could be cut off. Operator AI should limit WhatsApp agents to defined business tasks and keep a human handoff.

findings.title: Instagram DM automation runs into Meta API rate limits, such as 750 private replies to comments per hour per account
findings.detail: Meta's Messenger Platform rate-limit documentation sets per-second Send API ceilings for Instagram professional accounts and a cap of 750 private replies to comments per hour per Instagram professional account. That is the limit 'comment keyword to DM' automations usually hit. The often-quoted '200 per hour' is a misreading of the Facebook Page formula of 200 x engaged users per 24 hours. Vendor claims of about 50 comment-triggered DMs an hour are not in Meta's documentation.
findings.why_it_matters: Creator launches and challenge campaigns can produce thousands of comments in an hour. Operator AI's DM-setter queue needs throttling, prioritisation (hottest leads first) and visible backlog to stay within platform limits.

findings.title: YouTube: Video Action Campaigns are fully replaced by Demand Gen, which adds Discover, Gmail and Display inventory
findings.detail: Google removed new Video Action Campaign creation in April 2025, began automatic upgrades to Demand Gen in July 2025, and upgraded the last campaigns in April 2026. Demand Gen adds Discover, Gmail and the Google Display Network to YouTube; video partners can be opted out. Upgraded campaigns start paused. Lead forms were among the common causes of upgrade errors. Google claims, from internal 2024 data, similar conversions at similar CPA to Video Action Campaigns, and 20% more conversions at the same CPA when image assets are added to video.
findings.why_it_matters: Coaches running YouTube VSL or webinar acquisition must rebuild in Demand Gen and supply image assets alongside video. Operator AI's YouTube playbook and templates should assume Demand Gen and check lead-form compatibility.

findings.title: TikTok: Smart+ automation can now be switched on or off by module, and the US joint venture closed Jan 22, 2026 with ad tools unchanged
findings.detail: TikTok's undated Smart+ pages say advertisers can turn automation on or off separately for targeting, budget, catalog and placements, and choose placements manually. Lead generation runs through Instant Forms, web forms, and messaging and call ads, with Cost Cap bidding. On Jan 22, 2026, TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC acquired TikTok's US business (Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX hold 50% combined; ByteDance keeps 19.9%). Ads Manager and Smart+ reportedly run unchanged. The recommendation algorithm is being retrained on US data, which may shift ad delivery, and eMarketer frames 2026 as a recalibration year.
findings.why_it_matters: TikTok is less of a regulatory risk for creator-led coaching acquisition than in earlier years, but delivery may be unstable. Operator AI should treat TikTok as a test channel with module-level automation settings recorded per campaign.

findings.title: Meta lead-campaign cost benchmarks for 2026: about $27 per lead overall, about $26 for education (sample size not disclosed)
findings.detail: LocaliQ/WordStream 2026 Facebook benchmarks (page updated Sep 23, 2026), lead campaigns across 20 industries: CTR 2.70%, CPC $1.80, conversion rate 8.54%, CPL $27.39 (2025: $27.66). Education & Instruction: CPL $26.31, conversion rate 15.87%, CTR 1.74%. Career & Employment: CPL $12.30. The data window and sample size are not stated. Focus Digital, an agency (published Aug 21, 2026), analysed 138 North American Meta campaigns (Mar 3 - Jun 21, 2026; each with at least 50 conversions): spend-weighted CPL about $42, education $34.85. It gives no coaching category and no per-industry sample counts. Secondary roundups report Meta CPMs up roughly 13-20% year on year in 2026.
findings.why_it_matters: These are top-of-funnel form-fill costs, a weak proxy for high-ticket economics. Operator AI dashboards should show CPL only next to cost per qualified lead, per booked call, per shown call and per close.

findings.title: No independent benchmark exists for cost per booked call; published coaching figures are practitioner rules of thumb
findings.detail: No multi-account study of cost per booked call for coaching was found. One agency guide (undated) says $50-150 per booked call at $1,000-1,500 a month of spend, with 2-3 weeks to stabilise. A practitioner who says he has managed $12M+ in ad spend (Aug 17, 2024) treats under 5% of leads booking as a funnel problem, not an ad problem. He contrasts two VSL clients with 52% versus 21% of viewers still watching at the call-to-action, and argues that doubling retention at the call-to-action would roughly halve cost per call. That is illustrative maths, not a measured result. A Jul 13, 2025 review of 50+ high-ticket coaching VSLs gives qualitative patterns only: qualify hard, sell the call's outcome, use specific client stories.
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI should build tenant-level benchmarks from its own anonymised data (with consent) rather than quote internet ranges. The lack of public data is itself a gap the product can fill.

findings.title: High-ticket show and close rates: the best available figures are about 25% no-show and about 25% close on shown calls, mostly self-reported
findings.detail: A sales-recruiting firm's report (dated Mar 3, 2026) covering 273 high-ticket sales companies (2023-2026) puts the mean conversion of shown calls at about 25% and no-show at about 25%, both stable over the period, with life/mindset coaching converting at about 31%. The methodology is thin and the data likely self-reported. A closer job posting targets about 22% close and about 63% show. An agency price-band table (2025, no method given) shows 25.73% for $500-10k deals and 21.81% for $10-50k. Other vendor ranges run from 3-5% to 18%, and 5-12% as 'normal' for $2-10k DM sales. A Hyros page stated that no primary-source show-rate benchmark exists for high-ticket coaching funnels.
findings.why_it_matters: Students will ask what 'good' looks like. Operator AI should show these as wide, low-confidence reference bands, segment by lead source and price, and avoid presenting any as a standard.

findings.title: Show-rate drivers: B2B no-show data and a 77k-interview study suggest booking very soon is not always best
findings.detail: RevenueHero (scheduling vendor): an analysis of 6,428 B2B meetings in Dec 2024 found 6.5% no-show; an Aug 2025 analysis of companies booking 50+ meetings a month found a 15.9% average, 13.5% median and 5.5% for the top decile. Chili Piper is cited second-hand at 20-35%. Talview (recruiting vendor) analysed 77,589 interviews: those scheduled 24-72 hours ahead had 91-92% show, versus 71-72% for those scheduled within 24 hours. SegMetrics (vendor playbook) claims coaches booking same-week calls see 75%+ show versus about 50% for calls a week out, with no method. Reminder evidence for sales calls is mostly vendor claims, e.g. 30-40% fewer no-shows from automated reminders.
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI's booking and reminder logic should A/B test lead-time windows (same-day, 1-3 days, a week or more) and reminder cadence per tenant, not hard-code 'book ASAP'. Show rate by lead time is an obvious dashboard metric.

findings.title: Webinar attendance benchmarks are B2B platform data (about 40-60% of registrants); no controlled webinar-vs-VSL-vs-challenge comparisons exist for coaching
findings.detail: ON24's 2026 benchmarks (2025 platform data, B2B) report about 60% of registrants attending and 239 average attendees, up from 57% and 216. A Jul 8, 2026 ON24 update summarised by Quartr gives about 211 attendees, which conflicts. Contrast (2025) says about 6 in 10 registrants watch live or on demand. Goldcast reports 33% average attendance across 3.5M registrants in 2024. A B2B median live rate of about 41.6% is attributed inconsistently. Coaching figures are vendor claims only: 35-45% live show-up and 3-8% close for webinars versus 1-2% for cold discovery-call funnels; 5-day challenges converting 15-30% of participants; 10-20% of webinar attendees booking calls for $2k+ offers (single practitioner). SegMetrics sets a 50-70% application-to-call target; its worked example is 198 calls from 320 applications (61.9%).
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI should not claim one funnel type 'wins'. It should support side-by-side funnel experiments (webinar, VSL, challenge, DM-to-call) with the same stage definitions so each creator client gets real comparative data.

findings.title: Show-up email and SMS sequences: there is a minimum webinar reminder pattern, but lift evidence is mostly uncontrolled vendor cases
findings.detail: Vendor playbooks recommend at least four emails (confirmation, 24h, 1h, 'we're live') with new value in each, plus SMS the day before, the same morning, and about 10 minutes before start with a direct join link. Reported SMS lifts include one company going from about 25% to about 50% attendance, and a nearly 80% attendance rise with SMS opt-in growing from 12% to 25%. Neither had a control group. Better-quality evidence is from healthcare appointment reminders, where SMS modestly improves attendance (a Cochrane review reported a risk ratio of about 1.14, cited second-hand); that is a loose analogy.
findings.why_it_matters: Operator AI should ship reminder sequences as templates with built-in holdout tests, so each tenant measures its own lift. It should also capture SMS consent at registration, which affects compliance and reach.

findings.title: SMS reminder compliance: TCPA 'revoke-all' delayed to Jan 31, 2027, and several states set stricter quiet hours (8am-8pm)
findings.detail: The FCC's revocation-of-consent rule (47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10)) was due Apr 11, 2025. The 'revoke-all' part, under which an opt-out from one message type covers all future robocalls and robotexts from that sender, was delayed to Apr 11, 2026 and then, by order DA-26-12A on Jan 6, 2026, to Jan 31, 2027. Law-firm commentary reads the rest of the rule (accepting opt-outs by any reasonable means) as in force since April 2025. Florida, Oklahoma, Maryland and Washington set narrower calling windows than the federal 8am-9pm, around 8am-8pm in the recipient's time zone; Oklahoma also caps same-subject solicitations at three per 24h. A 2026 class action targets marketing texts sent before 8am.
findings.why_it_matters: Automated booking and reminder SMS from setters and AI agents need consent records, keyword plus natural-language opt-out handling, recipient-time-zone quiet hours and per-state rules. These belong in Operator AI's approval and policy layer.

findings.title: Email deliverability: Gmail stepped up bulk-sender enforcement from Nov 2025, and Outlook has required SPF, DKIM and DMARC since May 5, 2025
findings.detail: Google updated its bulk-sender FAQ in early Nov 2025 to say enforcement ramps up from that month. Senders of 5,000+ messages a day to Gmail that fail authentication, alignment, one-click unsubscribe, complaint-rate or RFC requirements now get temporary deferrals (4xx) and increasingly rejections (5xx), not just warnings. Microsoft has required SPF, DKIM and DMARC (at least p=none) since May 5, 2025 for domains sending more than 5,000 emails a day to Outlook.com, Hotmail and Live. Non-compliant mail goes to junk first and is expected to be rejected later.
findings.why_it_matters: Webinar and call reminder emails are time-critical; a deferred '1 hour to go' email is a lost show. Operator AI should check each tenant's sending-domain authentication and complaint rates during onboarding and before any launch sequence.

findings.title: FTC moved to enforcement of its Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule, which covers the testimonial-heavy content in coaching funnels
findings.detail: On Dec 22, 2025 the FTC sent warning letters to 10 companies under the Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule (16 CFR Part 465), asking for written confirmation of corrective steps within 5 days. The targets included testimonials that misrepresent the reviewer's experience, and incentives conditioned on what a review says. Law firms note the Rule lets the FTC seek civil penalties (cited at up to about $53,088 per violation, inflation-adjusted) directly in federal court. Letters continued into 2026. No litigated penalty under the Rule was found.
findings.why_it_matters: Student case studies, client wins and screenshot proof drive VSLs, webinars and DM scripts. Operator AI should tag each testimonial with consent, any incentive, and whether results are typical, and block unverified testimonials from publishing without approval.

I found no independent multi-account dataset on show rates, close rates, or cost per booked or shown call for high-ticket coaching funnels by funnel type (webinar, VSL, challenge, DM-to-call). Would tenants consent to anonymised pooled benchmarks inside Operator AI to fill this gap?
Could Meta's Conversion Leads (CRM stage) optimisation extend beyond Instant Forms to website or VSL funnels? Today those funnels can only send custom events through CAPI.
What do Instagram and Messenger policies require for disclosing AI-run DM conversations to leads, and when must a human take over? I found no primary Meta guidance.

briefs.title: Say 'AI assistant' at first contact on the phone line and on Telegram, Slack, SMS and email Coach replies
briefs.why: Out of compliance today. channels.voice_call greets callers with 'Hi, ask me anything about the programme.' (channels.py:590) and never says it is an AI. Our own playbooks require disclosure: compliance-2026 'ai-disclosure-bots-voice-clones' and sales-setting-closing 'ai-setter-disclosure-and-handoff'. EU AI Act Art. 50(1) has applied since 2026-08-02 and the Digital Omnibus did not delay it (Jones Walker 2026-07-16; Cloud Security Alliance 2026-07-29). California BOT Act, Bus. & Prof. Code 17941. Meta Messenger Platform policy asks for bot disclosure at the start, after a long gap, and when switching from a human to automation (developers.facebook.com, accessed 2026-10-27).
briefs.build:
Backend:
(1) channels.voice_call greeting: 'You're speaking with {brand}'s automated AI assistant, not a person. Say human at any time to leave a message for the team.' A spoken human, agent or person queues a callback item for the owner. It never places a call itself.
(2) New helper persona/apply.disclosure_line(tenant, channel). inbound._coach_reply prefixes '[Automated AI assistant for {brand}]' on the first reply in a thread, after a gap of 24h or more, and after a human reply in the same thread.
(3) Fixed honest answer to 'are you a bot/human/real?'.
(4) guardrails: new check 'missing_ai_disclosure' on AI-authored channel_reply, setter_reply and booking_dm items whose thread has no disclosed message yet. It blocks at approve and again at send.
(5) settings: API-editable 'ai_disclosure_line', max 160 characters, must contain 'AI' or 'automated'.
UI: Channels.tsx shows the line and a preview.
Tests: tests/test_ai_disclosure.py covers TwiML containing 'AI assistant'; first reply prefixed, second within 24h not, prefixed again after 25h; honest bot answer; guardrail block; an invalid disclosure setting returns 422. Update the expectations in test_voice_line.py.
Touches: channels.py, inbound.py, persona/apply.py, guardrails.py, settings.py, Channels.tsx, docs/GUARDRAILS.md.
briefs.acceptance: New tests pass and the full suite is green. No code path speaks or sends an AI-authored first message without the disclosure line. GUARDRAILS.md documents missing_ai_disclosure. The owner can reword the disclosure but cannot remove it.
briefs.must_not: No cloned or person-like voice: NEUTRAL_TTS_VOICES stays. Never imply the AI is the coach or a human. Channel replies stay approval-gated: no auto-send, no auto-approve. No outbound AI calls.

briefs.title: Minis: AI disclosure, scoped-retrieval bug, pause/expire/delete, abuse caps, consented leads
briefs.why:
Out of date and buggy.
- MINI_HTML (routes/channels.py:140) says only 'Answers come only from the programme's material.' It has no AI disclosure, which EU AI Act Art. 50 requires from 2026-08-02 (compliance-2026 'ai-disclosure-bots-voice-clones').
- console._scoped_answer searches k=40 across the whole corpus and only then filters to the mini's files (console.py:296). On a large corpus the mini's own files get crowded out and it wrongly answers 'outside what this assistant covers'.
- A mini cannot be paused, expired or deleted.
- Captured emails never become leads.
- Jeremy runs time-limited webinar, challenge and sales-page 'instances' with verified email and usage caps (jeremyhaynes.com 2026-04-09).
briefs.build:
Backend:
- MINI_HTML and the first answer say: 'Automated AI assistant trained on {brand}'s material. Not a person.'
- _scoped_answer calls retrieval.search(files=scope) from B2. Until B2 merges, fall back to k = min(400, passages_in_scope*3).
- minis gain status (active, paused, expired), expires_at and max_sessions. PATCH and DELETE (soft delete with audit) in routes/owner.py. Public routes return 410 when expired or paused and 404 when deleted.
- Abuse controls without sending anything: tighter per-IP and per-email daily caps, a disposable-domain blocklist, and a honeypot field.
- On consent, emit events.emit('lead_captured', {source:'mini', slug, email, consent_text_version, ts}) and mark the lead 'unverified'. Minis.tsx lists the leads; 'Draft follow-up' creates a queue item of kind 'followup' (approval-gated).
Tests: tests/test_minis.py covers disclosure in the HTML; a 3,000-passage corpus where a 2-file mini still answers from its files; 410 and 404 states; the event emitted with the consent version; no email sent at capture.
briefs.acceptance: Mini answers stay correct on large corpora. Owners can pause, expire and delete minis. Leads appear only with consent. Every mini page and first answer discloses AI.
briefs.must_not: No VPN or IP fingerprinting. No verification codes by email or SMS, because that would be an unapproved send. No contact with captured emails without queue approval. public_line_ok's money-figure block stays.

briefs.title: Member plan changes, a dunning grace period, recurring-billing compliance and seat entitlements; fix the Drive staging collision
briefs.why:
Buggy and out of date.
- console.payment_webhook's upsert runs 'ON CONFLICT(email) DO UPDATE SET status, updated' (console.py:153), so plan upgrades and downgrades are dropped.
- payment.failed deactivates a student at once.
- If seats are sold as recurring plans, compliance-2026 'subscriptions-auto-renewal' applies (ROSCA; California BPC 17602: consent records kept 3 years, online cancellation, renewal reminders), as does fulfilment-retention-ops 'dispute-prevention-billing-hygiene'.
- Jeremy sells at $1K/mo or $10K/yr with seat discounts (jeremyhaynesai.com, accessed 2026-10-27).
- drive_decide writes '<stem>.txt', so call.pdf and call.docx overwrite each other.
briefs.build:
Backend:
- The upsert sets plan, status, updated and period_end.
- payment.failed sets past_due with grace_until = now + grace_days (default 7, stored in billing.py's table). Deactivation is checked lazily via billing.active(user) at login or request.
- billing.py:
  - Plans: {interval month|year, seats, entitlements: coach, role-play minutes, voice minutes, minis}, with seat counts per tenant.
  - Renewal-reminder drafts go into the queue as kind 'reminder': 15-45 days before an annual renewal, and 3-21 days before the end of a trial or promotion longer than 31 days.
  - Consent records {terms_version, ts, ip, method} kept at least 3 years.
  - Online cancel page at /t/<tid>/billing/cancel, two clicks or fewer.
  - Emits events payment_received and payment_refunded {amount, currency, email, source} for C2.
